source: UNOOSA National Space Law database and official legislation portals / gazettes (verified 24 September 2026)
classification_rule: yes = an enacted, in-force instrument with binding legal force (statute, or binding regulation/decree) establishes an authorisation regime for non-governmental space activities (remote-sensing-only regimes count and are flagged); no = no such regime (agency-creation, registration-only, telecoms/spectrum-only, State monopoly without private authorisation, or drafts only); consortium = intergovernmental organisation, company or multi-State programme code; unknown = not determinable.

US.instrument: Commercial Space Launch Act 1984 as amended (51 U.S.C. ch. 509; 14 CFR Parts 440, 450); Land Remote Sensing Policy Act 1992 (15 CFR 960); Communications Act 1934 with FCC 47 CFR Part 25

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Act, Pub. L. 98-575 (1984), as amended, codified at 51 U.S.C. ch. 509 (§§50901-50924)
instruments.note: FAA licenses launch, re-entry and sites (US citizens anywhere; anyone in US); payload review §50904(c); insurance/cross-waivers §50914; indemnification §50915. Code current to Pub. L. 119-111.

instruments.name: 14 CFR Part 450, Launch and Reentry License Requirements (Streamlined Launch and Reentry License Requirements final rule, 85 FR 79566, Dec. 10, 2020)
instruments.note: Performance-based vehicle operator licence, effective 10 Mar 2021. Legacy Parts 415/417/431/435 removed 10 Mar 2026, so Part 450 is the sole vehicle licence. §450.171 orbital debris rules.

instruments.name: 14 CFR Part 440, Financial Responsibility
instruments.note: Maximum probable loss-based third-party liability insurance, US Government property cover and reciprocal waivers of claims for licensed launch/re-entry; implements 51 U.S.C. 50914 (Art VII).

instruments.name: 14 CFR chapter III, Commercial Space Transportation (Parts 400-460 other than 440 and 450: incl. 401, 404, 405, 413, 414, 420, 433, 437, 460)
instruments.note: Application procedure (413), safety element approvals (414), launch/re-entry site licences (420, 433), experimental permits (437), human spaceflight crew/participant rules (460), enforcement (405).

instruments.name: Land Remote Sensing Policy Act of 1992, Pub. L. 102-555, codified at 51 U.S.C. ch. 601 (§§60101-60162)
instruments.note: §60121: Commerce (NOAA/Office of Space Commerce) licenses private remote sensing space systems; conditions incl. satellite disposal and national-security limits. Amended 1998, 2010, 2015.

instruments.name: 15 CFR Part 960, Licensing of Private Remote Sensing Space Systems (final rule, 85 FR 30790, May 20, 2020)
instruments.note: Tiered (1-3) licensing by capability; effective 20 July 2020; no amendments since per eCFR. Temporary Tier-3 conditions expire after 3 years. Replaced 2006 rules.

instruments.name: Communications Act of 1934, 47 U.S.C. §151 et seq., Title III (47 U.S.C. §§301-399), incl. §§301, 303, 308, 309, 310
instruments.note: No radio transmission without FCC licence (§301): the FCC space-station licence or market-access grant is how nearly all US non-governmental satellites are authorised; §310 foreign ownership limits.

instruments.name: 47 CFR Part 25, Satellite Communications
instruments.note: FCC space/earth station licensing and US market access; §25.114(d)(14) debris showings; §25.283 end-of-life disposal. Latest eCFR revision 31 Jul 2026. To be replaced by Part 100.

instruments.name: 47 CFR Part 5 (Experimental Radio Service) and Part 97 (Amateur Radio Service, satellite provisions)
instruments.note: Alternative FCC routes for many small, academic and experimental satellites; carry the same orbital-debris showings (§5.64, §97.207) as amended in 2020-2024.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Act Amendments of 1988, Pub. L. 100-657
instruments.note: Created the MPL insurance, cross-waiver and government payment-of-excess-claims (indemnification) regime now at 51 U.S.C. 50914-50915.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Act of 1998, Pub. L. 105-303
instruments.note: Extended ch. 509 licensing to re-entry vehicles and re-entry sites; amended remote-sensing licensing provisions.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Amendments Act of 2004, Pub. L. 108-492
instruments.note: Added experimental permits and regime for crew and space flight participants (informed consent) and the human-spaceflight regulatory 'learning period' (51 U.S.C. 50905(c)).

instruments.name: U.S. Commercial Space Launch Competitiveness Act, Pub. L. 114-90, Title I (SPACE Act of 2015)
instruments.note: Extended indemnification and learning period, extended cross-waivers to government astronauts, added government-astronaut provisions and FAA report duties. Title III renamed Office of Space Commerce.

instruments.name: Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025, Pub. L. 118-159, div. E, §5702
instruments.note: Latest extensions: learning period to 1 Jan 2028 (§50905(c)(9)); indemnification to licences applied for by 30 Sep 2028 (§50915(f)). Prior stopgaps: Pub. L. 118-15, 118-34, 118-41, 118-63 §1111.

instruments.name: Space Resource Exploration and Utilization Act of 2015, Pub. L. 114-90, Title IV, codified at 51 U.S.C. ch. 513 (§§51301-51303)
instruments.note: Grants US citizens rights to space resources obtained under applicable law; §51302 directs facilitation subject to authorisation and continuing supervision, but creates no licensing process.

instruments.name: FCC Mitigation of Orbital Debris in the New Space Age, Report and Order, FCC 20-54 (85 FR 52422, 2020), and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 24-6 (89 FR 13276, 2024)
instruments.note: Collision-risk (<0.001), casualty-risk, trackability, maneuverability and ownership disclosures in Part 25/5/97 applications; key §25.114(d)(14) changes effective 9 Sep 2024 (89 FR 65217).

instruments.name: FCC Space Innovation; Mitigation of Orbital Debris in the New Space Age, Second Report and Order, FCC 22-74 (IB Dkt 22-271, 18-313) - five-year post-mission disposal rule, 47 CFR 25.283(e)
instruments.note: LEO satellites (<2000 km) using uncontrolled re-entry must deorbit within 5 years of mission end. Effective 9 Sep 2024; compliance from 29 Sep 2024 (89 FR 65217); earlier satellites grandfathered.

instruments.name: FCC Protecting Our Communications Networks by Promoting Transparency Regarding Foreign Adversary Control, Report and Order, FCC 26-2 (91 FR 18670, Apr. 10, 2026)
instruments.note: Effective 9 Jun 2026: all Part 25 applicants/holders must attest whether under foreign adversary control (47 CFR part 1, incl. §1.80003; compliance date to be announced).

instruments.name: FCC Space Modernization for the 21st Century, Report and Order and FNPRM, FCC 26-47 (SB Docket No. 25-306), new 47 CFR Part 100 'Space and Earth Station Services'
instruments.note: Adopted 22 Jul 2026; replaces Part 25 (sunset on effect). Part 100 rules effective only after OMB review and FR notice; not in FR/eCFR as of 24 Sep 2026. Keeps 5-year deorbit certification.

instruments.name: U.S. national registry of space objects maintained by the Department of State (notified under Art. II Registration Convention, ST/SG/SER.E/INF.3, 1977)
instruments.note: No statute: State Dept (OES Office of Space Affairs) compiles data from DoD, NASA, FAA and sends to UN by note verbale; latest listed ST/SG/SER.E/1302 (2025). Reg. Convention ratified 1976.

instruments.name: National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958, Pub. L. 85-568, codified at 51 U.S.C. ch. 201
instruments.note: Establishes NASA and its powers for government space activities; not a licensing statute and confers no authority over private operators.

instruments.name: An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14 ('One Big Beautiful Bill Act'), Pub. L. 119-21, §40004
instruments.note: Added 51 U.S.C. 50924: per-launch/re-entry licensing and permitting user fees from 2026, paid into an FAA/AST fund; FAA policy statement on fees 91 FR 21591 (22 Apr 2026).

instruments.name: Executive Order 14335 of August 13, 2025, Enabling Competition in the Commercial Space Industry (90 FR 40219)
instruments.note: Directs FAA to streamline Part 450 and environmental review, elevates Office of Space Commerce, and (sec. 5) orders Commerce to propose mission authorisation for Art VI activities not covered today.

instruments.name: U.S. Government Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices (2019 update)
instruments.note: Governs USG-sponsored missions and is a benchmark for FAA/FCC debris review; not binding on private licensees except as incorporated into licence rules or conditions.

instruments.name: FAA Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, Waiver of Specified Statutory Requirements for Commercial Space Launch and Reentry Actions (91 FR 47997, July 30, 2026; Docket FAA-2026-8614)
instruments.note: Proposes using 51 U.S.C. 50905(b)(2)(C) waiver power to waive 13 environmental and related statutes for Parts 420/433/437/450 authorisations; comments closed 31 Aug 2026.

instruments.name: Office of Space Commerce, Notice of Mission Authorization Pilot Program - Space Commerce Certification (91 FR 53849, Aug. 20, 2026)
instruments.note: Voluntary, non-statutory mission-authorisation framework for novel in-space activities under EO 14335 sec. 5; pilot expressions of interest due 5 Oct 2026. No legal authority yet.

instruments.name: Secure Space Act of 2026, S. 1962, 119th Congress (House companion: Secure Space Act of 2025, H.R. 2458)
instruments.note: Bars FCC satellite licences/market access/earth-station grants to covered-list entities and affiliates. H.R. 2458 passed House 28 Apr 2025; S. 1962 passed Senate amended 23 Sep 2026. Not enacted.

instruments.name: ORBITS Act of 2025, S. 1898, 119th Congress
instruments.note: Active debris-removal demonstration and uniform orbital debris standard practices. Reported by Senate Commerce 18 Jun 2026 (S. Rept. 119-128). Predecessor S. 447 (118th) passed Senate 2023, lapsed.

instruments.name: LAUNCH Act (Licensing Aerospace Units to New Commercial Heights), S. 1961 / H.R. 5602, 119th Congress
instruments.note: Would streamline ch. 509 launch/re-entry licensing and ch. 601 remote-sensing licensing. Introduced 5 Jun 2025 (S.) and 26 Sep 2025 (H.R.); no committee action.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Act of 2023, H.R. 6131, 118th Congress
instruments.note: Would have given Commerce mission authorisation (certification) of novel activities and reformed remote sensing. Ordered reported 29 Nov 2023; lapsed Jan 2025. No 119th reintroduction found.

considered_not_relevant.name: Artemis Accords (2020)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Non-binding political statement of principles among signatory States; not legislation and creates no national authorisation, registration or liability rule.

considered_not_relevant.name: Executive Order 14369 of December 18, 2025, Ensuring American Space Superiority (90 FR 60537)
considered_not_relevant.reason: National space policy direction (and revision of SPD-3 on space traffic data); creates no authorisation, registration or liability rule for operators.

considered_not_relevant.name: Space Policy Directive-3 (2018), National Space Traffic Management Policy / Commerce TraCSS
considered_not_relevant.reason: Policy and a voluntary SSA data service; not a licensing or supervision instrument.

considered_not_relevant.name: FAA NPRM, Mitigation Methods for Launch Vehicle Upper Stages on the Creation of Orbital Debris (88 FR 65835, 2023)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Withdrawn effective 15 Jan 2026 (91 FR 1724); never adopted.

considered_not_relevant.name: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (22 CFR 120-130) and Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR 730-774)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Export controls on space technology; do not authorise or supervise space objects.

considered_not_relevant.name: NASA Transition Authorization Act (S. 933) / NASA Reauthorization Act of 2026 (H.R. 7273)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Pending NASA programme authorisation bills; no commercial licensing, registry or liability provisions identified.

considered_not_relevant.name: H.R. 5174 (119th), revisions to keep title 51 U.S.C. current
considered_not_relevant.reason: Technical codification bill (passed House; referred to Senate Judiciary 14 Sep 2026); no substantive change to licensing regimes.

considered_not_relevant.name: 51 U.S.C. ch. 511 (Space transportation infrastructure matching grants) and SPACEPORT Act (H.R. 5447)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Spaceport funding; no authorisation or supervision function.

considered_not_relevant.name: Secure U.S. Leadership in Space Act of 2025 (S. 1560 / H.R. 3142)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Tax-exempt financing for spaceports; unrelated to authorisation of space objects.

considered_not_relevant.name: FCC NPRM 'Spectrum Abundance for Weird Space Stuff' (91 FR, Apr. 9, 2026)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Spectrum-allocation proposal for novel missions; pending and does not itself create an authorisation regime beyond Part 25/100.

CIS.instrument: Law No. 5663-1 'On Space Activities' (1993, as amended to Federal Law No. 540-FZ of 2025), with Regulation on Licensing of Space Activities (Gov. Decree No. 168 of 2022) and Roscosmos registry order

instruments.name: Law of the Russian Federation No. 5663-1 of 20 August 1993 'On Space Activities' (as amended)
instruments.note: Art. 9: space activity licensed under Law 99-FZ (2011). Art. 17: registration of space objects. Also insurance and liability. Last amended by 540-FZ (2025). UNOOSA text is an older English version.

instruments.name: Government Decree No. 168 of 14 February 2022 approving the Regulation on Licensing of Space Activities
instruments.note: Licensing by Roscosmos. In force 1 Sep 2022 until 1 Sep 2028. Amended by Decrees No. 252 (2024), No. 1271 (2025) and No. 68 (2026).

instruments.name: Roscosmos Order No. 411 of 11 December 2025 on the procedure for registering launched space objects and maintaining the national register
instruments.note: Current rules for the national register of launched space objects kept by Roscosmos. Replaces earlier registry rules. Exact entry-into-force date not verified.

instruments.name: Federal Law No. 540-FZ of 29 December 2025 amending the Law 'On Space Activities' and the Federal Law on Roscosmos
instruments.note: Latest amendment. Among other things it regulates Roscosmos acquisition of remote-sensing data from non-state spacecraft for public bodies. Some provisions take effect 28 Jun 2026.

instruments.name: Federal Law No. 215-FZ of 13 July 2015 'On the State Corporation for Space Activities Roscosmos'
instruments.note: Establishes Roscosmos as the licensing authority, registry keeper and UN registration channel. Amended by 540-FZ (2025).

instruments.name: Roscosmos Order No. 411 of 3 December 2024 on the procedure for providing Earth remote sensing data and products
instruments.note: Procedure for providing remote-sensing data, copies and products from the federal fund. Data dissemination only, not operator licensing.

considered_not_relevant.name: Federal Law No. 126-FZ 'On Communications' (2003)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Spectrum and telecom licensing. It is not the mechanism for authorising space activities, which Roscosmos licenses.

PRC.borderline: No statute: the licensing and registration regime rests on departmental rules (bumen guizhang) of COSTIND (now SASTIND/CNSA). These are binding secondary legislation, so 'yes' holds, but the national Space Law is still only in draft.
PRC.instrument: Interim Measures on Permits for Civil Space Launch Projects (COSTIND Order No. 12, 2002) and Space Object Registration Measures (Order No. 6, 2001), plus SASTIND 2019/2023 notices; Space Law still draft

instruments.name: Interim Measures on the Administration of Permits for Civil Space Launch Projects (COSTIND Order No. 12)
instruments.note: Licence needed for civil launches from China and for Chinese-owned spacecraft launched abroad (incl. in-orbit delivery). In force 21 Dec 2002. Administered by SASTIND/CNSA.

instruments.name: Measures for the Administration of Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space (COSTIND/MFA Order No. 6)
instruments.note: National registry of space objects, implementing the Registration Convention. Covers objects launched from China and those where China is a co-launching State. In force 8 Feb 2001.

instruments.name: SASTIND Notice on Strengthening the Administration of Civil Space Launch Project Permits (23 Feb 2023)
instruments.note: Applications must include TPL insurance, a space radio station licence and a debris-mitigation plan. Requires end-of-life deorbit and registration within 30 days of launch, with change registration.

instruments.name: SASTIND/CMC Equipment Development Dept Notice on Promoting the Standardised and Orderly Development of Commercial Launch Vehicles (Ke Gong Yi Si [2019] No. 647)
instruments.note: Commercial launch vehicle R&D, testing, launch and safety controls. Sounding and suborbital launches must be filed with SASTIND (per 2023 notice).

instruments.name: CNSA Notice on Strengthening Quality Supervision and Administration of Commercial Space Projects (16 Jul 2025)
instruments.note: Whole-life-cycle quality supervision of commercial space projects, including launch, operation, recovery and disposal. A launch permit is required before launch activity.

instruments.name: Regulations of the PRC on Radio Administration (State Council/CMC Decree No. 672, revised 2016)
instruments.note: Space radio station licensing and satellite frequency and orbit use. In force 1 Dec 2016.

instruments.name: MIIT Measures for Satellite Network Filing, Coordination, Registration and Maintenance (Trial)
instruments.note: Domestic procedure for ITU filings and coordination of satellite networks.

instruments.name: CNSA Interim Measures for International Cooperation on National Civil Satellite Remote Sensing Data
instruments.note: Governs international sharing and provision of civil satellite EO data. Not an operator licensing regime.

instruments.name: CNSA Action Plan to Promote the High-Quality and Safe Development of Commercial Space (2025-2027)
instruments.note: Policy plan (Nov 2025) to unify regulatory standards and streamline launch approvals. Not legislation. CNSA set up a Commercial Space Department in Nov 2025.

instruments.name: Space Law of the PRC (draft)
instruments.note: State Council 2026 Legislative Work Plan lists the Space Law draft as 'preparatory' for submission to the NPC Standing Committee. It has not been submitted or enacted.

considered_not_relevant.name: National Security Law of the PRC (2015), Art. 32
considered_not_relevant.reason: Declares security interests in outer space. It creates no authorisation, registry or liability mechanism.

considered_not_relevant.name: Commercial Space Standards System (Version 1.0), CNSA/SAMR, April 2026
considered_not_relevant.reason: Technical standards framework, not a binding authorisation instrument.

UK.instrument: Outer Space Act 1986 (UK entities' activities abroad) and Space Industry Act 2018 (activities in the UK), with Space Industry Regulations 2021; liability terms amended by Space Industry (Indemnities) Act 2025

instruments.name: Outer Space Act 1986 (c. 38)
instruments.note: Licensing of UK nationals/companies' space activities outside the UK; register of space objects (s.7); indemnity to Government (s.10); licence insurance (€60m standard). Amended by SIA 2018 & DA 2015.

instruments.name: Space Industry Act 2018 (c. 5)
instruments.note: Licenses spaceflight activities in the UK (launch, sub-orbital, orbital operator, spaceport, range control); operator liability ss.34-36; commenced 29 July 2021. Amended by 2025 Indemnities Act.

instruments.name: The Space Industry Regulations 2021 (S.I. 2021/792)
instruments.note: Detailed licensing, safety, security, orbital-operator and insurance rules under SIA 2018; appoints CAA as regulator (Part 2). In force 29 July 2021; amended by S.I. 2025/222.

instruments.name: Space Industry (Indemnities) Act 2025 (c. 35)
instruments.note: Amends SIA 2018 s.12 so every operator licence must specify a limit on the licensee's s.36 indemnity to Government. Royal Assent 18 Dec 2025; in force 18 Feb 2026 (two months after passing).

instruments.name: Deregulation Act 2015 (c. 20), section 12 (amending Outer Space Act 1986 s.10)
instruments.note: Requires OSA licences to specify a limit on the licensee's indemnity to Government; basis of the €60m standard orbital liability cap.

instruments.name: The Contracting Out (Functions in Relation to Space) Order 2021 (S.I. 2021/815)
instruments.note: Lets the Secretary of State authorise the CAA to exercise OSA 1986 functions (licensing, variation/revocation, directions, register of space objects). In force 29 July 2021.

instruments.name: The Space Industry (Appeals) Regulations 2021 (S.I. 2021/816)
instruments.note: Appeal procedure against CAA licensing and enforcement decisions under SIA 2018.

instruments.name: The Spaceflight Activities (Investigation of Spaceflight Accidents) Regulations 2021 (S.I. 2021/793)
instruments.note: Establishes independent investigation of spaceflight accidents under SIA 2018 (safety oversight).

instruments.name: The Space Industry (Licence Exemption for Military Activities of Allies) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/222)
instruments.note: Exempts authorised allied military sub-orbital activities and MoD range contractors from SIA licensing; amends SIR 2021 'space site' definition. In force 28 Feb 2025.

instruments.name: Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 (c. 36)
instruments.note: Basis for Ofcom satellite/space-station and earth-station licences and UK ITU satellite filings; parallel to CAA space licensing.

instruments.name: UK Government space regulatory financial reforms: variable liability limits for orbital operations (announced with UK Space Strategy, 18 Sept 2026)
instruments.note: Policy (not legislation): replaces flat €60m orbital cap with sustainability-linked variable limits via licence conditions; ISAM/lunar liability waived to 2030. Follows 2023 UKSA consultation.

considered_not_relevant.name: National Security and Investment Act 2021
considered_not_relevant.reason: Investment screening (satellite and space technologies is a mandatory-notification sector), but it does not authorise or supervise space objects.

considered_not_relevant.name: Export Control Act 2002 / Export Control Order 2008
considered_not_relevant.reason: Controls export of space items; no authorisation or supervision of space activities.

JPN.instrument: Space Activities Act (Act No. 76 of 2016; amended by Act No. 39 of 2026, mostly not yet in force), Remote Sensing Act (Act No. 77 of 2016) and Space Resources Act (Act No. 83 of 2021), under the Basic Space Act 2008

instruments.name: Act on Launching of Spacecraft, etc. and Control of Spacecraft (Act No. 76 of 2016)
instruments.note: Launch permits, spacecraft-control permits, strict liability, mandatory insurance and government indemnity. In force 15 Nov 2018. Title and scope change once Act No. 39 of 2026 takes effect.

instruments.name: Act Partially Amending the Act on Launching of Spacecraft, etc. and Control of Spacecraft and Other Acts (Act No. 39 of 2026)
instruments.note: Promulgated 17 Jun 2026. Renames Act 76 (Launching of Space Rockets and Control of Specified Satellites). Adds re-entry, test launches and on-orbit services. Mostly in force by 16 Jun 2027.

instruments.name: Act on Ensuring Appropriate Handling of Satellite Remote Sensing Records (Act No. 77 of 2016)
instruments.note: Licensing of satellite remote-sensing instrument operators and certification of data handlers. In force 2017-18. Not amended by Act No. 39 of 2026.

instruments.name: Act on the Promotion of Business Activities Related to the Exploration and Development of Space Resources (Act No. 83 of 2021)
instruments.note: Adds permits for space-resource activities to the spacecraft-control permit scheme. In force 23 Dec 2021. Amended by Act No. 39 of 2026 (not yet in force).

instruments.name: Regulation for Enforcement of the Act on Launching of Spacecraft, etc. and Control of Spacecraft (Cabinet Office Order No. 50 of 2017)
instruments.note: Detailed permit criteria, including debris-mitigation and end-of-life disposal requirements for spacecraft control. Last amended 2021.

instruments.name: Regulation for Enforcement of the Act on Ensuring Appropriate Handling of Satellite Remote Sensing Records (Cabinet Office Order No. 41 of 2017)
instruments.note: Detailed licensing criteria and data-handling rules. Last amended by Cabinet Office Order No. 50 of 2025.

instruments.name: Basic Space Act (Act No. 43 of 2008)
instruments.note: Framework law. Art. 35 mandates legislation to implement treaties. Amended by Act No. 39 of 2026 (in force on promulgation, 17 Jun 2026).

instruments.name: Radio Act (Act No. 131 of 1950)
instruments.note: Licensing of satellite radio stations by MIC. Last amended by Act No. 27 of 2026.

considered_not_relevant.name: Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act
considered_not_relevant.reason: Export control. It does not authorise or supervise space objects.

TBD.instrument: No attributed owner: SATCAT objects (mostly debris or unidentified objects) that 18 SDS/CelesTrak have not yet associated with a State or organisation; no legal framework can be assigned

FR.instrument: Law No. 2008-518 on Space Operations (LOS), as amended (2022, 2023, 2026), with Decree No. 2009-643 and the technical regulation (Order of 31 March 2011, updated 28 June 2024)

instruments.name: Law No. 2008-518 of 3 June 2008 on Space Operations (Loi relative aux opérations spatiales, LOS)
instruments.note: Prior authorisation of launches/in-orbit control from France or by French operators; CNES technical control; liability, insurance & State guarantee; Title VII space data. Amended 2022, 2023, 2026.

instruments.name: Decree No. 2009-643 of 9 June 2009 on authorisations issued under Law No. 2008-518 on space operations
instruments.note: Authorisation/licence procedure (4-month decision), CNES conformity checks, financial-guarantee proof, defence review. Amended by Decree 2022-234 and Decree 2024-625 (from 1 July 2024).

instruments.name: Order of 31 March 2011 on the technical regulation under Decree No. 2009-643 (Réglementation technique, RT)
instruments.note: Binding technical rules: launch safety, casualty-risk limits, debris mitigation, end-of-life disposal. Amended by orders of 23 Feb 2022 (in force 1 Jan 2023) and 28 June 2024.

instruments.name: Order of 28 June 2024 amending the Order of 31 March 2011 on the technical regulation (NOR ECOI2413938A)
instruments.note: 2024 RT update (requests from 1 July 2024): mega-constellation disposal (P≥0.95, 2-5 yr), reusable launchers, in-orbit servicing, no intentional fragmentation; transitional relief to 2028.

instruments.name: Decree No. 2024-625 of 28 June 2024 amending the provisions on authorisations of space operations
instruments.note: Amends Decree 2009-643 after LPM 2023: constellations, controlled stage returns, reusable launchers, in-orbit services; in force 1 July 2024.

instruments.name: Order of 23 February 2022 on the composition of the three parts of the file under Art. 1 of Decree No. 2009-643 (amended by Order of 28 June 2024)
instruments.note: Specifies the administrative, technical and mission file required for LOS authorisation applications.

instruments.name: Ordinance No. 2022-232 of 23 February 2022 on the protection of national defence interests in the conduct of space operations and the exploitation of space-based data
instruments.note: Amends LOS: defence grounds to refuse authorisation, derogations for State/defence missions, requisition of space assets, wider 'space-origin data' definition, criminal penalties.

instruments.name: Law No. 2023-703 of 1 August 2023 on military programming for 2024-2030, Art. 60
instruments.note: Amends LOS to bring satellite constellations and controlled return of launcher stages within the authorisation regime.

instruments.name: Law No. 2026-791 of 16 August 2026 updating military programming for 2024-2030 and on various defence provisions, Arts. 28 and 56
instruments.note: Verified real (JORF 18 Aug 2026). Amends LOS Art. 25-1 (exemptions from space-data rules) and creates Art. 25-2 (offence for space data over sensitive zones); in force 19 Aug 2026.

instruments.name: Decree No. 2009-640 of 9 June 2009 implementing Title VII of Law No. 2008-518 (space-origin data)
instruments.note: Declaration and control regime for primary operators of space-origin (Earth observation) data; amended by Decree 2022-233; Order of 4 Sept 2013 on declarations.

instruments.name: Research Code (Code de la recherche), Arts. L331-1 to L331-8 and R331-1 to R331-26 (CNES), with Order of 12 August 2011 on space-object identification information
instruments.note: CNES missions incl. keeping the French national registry of space objects on behalf of the State and technical control/CSG safety powers.

instruments.name: Postal and Electronic Communications Code, Art. L97-2 (satellite frequency assignments)
instruments.note: ANFR files and manages French satellite-network frequency assignments with the ITU on operators' request, subject to ministerial authorisation.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Would overlay LOS for EU operators.

considered_not_relevant.name: Defence Code export-control provisions (war materiel)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Export control of space items; no authorisation/supervision of space objects.

IND.borderline: IN-SPACe authorises non-governmental space activity in practice under the Indian Space Policy 2023 and its 2024 Norms, Guidelines and Procedures. These are executive instruments with no statutory basis or force of law, so the result is 'no' under the strict rule. The Space Activities Bill is still unintroduced.
IND.instrument: No space statute. IN-SPACe authorises under the non-statutory Indian Space Policy 2023 and IN-SPACe NGP (2024). Spectrum under Telecommunications Act 2023. Space Activities Bill redrafted 2025, not introduced

instruments.name: Indian Space Policy - 2023 (Department of Space)
instruments.note: Cabinet-approved policy. Gives IN-SPACe the role of authorising space activities of government and non-government entities. Operative basis of supervision but not law.

instruments.name: IN-SPACe Norms, Guidelines and Procedures for Implementation of Indian Space Policy-2023 in respect of Authorization of Space Activities (IN:ISP2023:NGP2024/V1.0)
instruments.note: Issued 3 May 2024. Authorisation of space objects, launch, re-entry, ground systems and EO data dissemination, including debris and liability conditions. Executive guidelines, not statutory.

instruments.name: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 (No. 44 of 2023)
instruments.note: Administrative assignment of spectrum for satellite services and authorisation of telecom services. Statutory, but covers telecoms and spectrum only.

instruments.name: Space Activities Bill (redrafted 2025)
instruments.note: First published 2017. Redrafted and finalised 2025 to give IN-SPACe statutory powers. Not introduced in Parliament; absent from Monsoon Session 2026 bills.

considered_not_relevant.name: FDI Policy amendment for the space sector (Press Note 1 of 2024)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Foreign investment caps. It does not authorise or supervise space objects.

ITSO.borderline: ITSO is an IGO that no longer operates satellites; the privatised Intelsat fleet (owned by SES since July 2025) is licensed mainly by the US FCC, with the US as registering State for those objects.
ITSO.instrument: ITSO Agreement (1971, in force 1973; restructured 2001); Intelsat fleet (SES since July 2025) licensed mainly by the US FCC under the Communications Act and 47 CFR Part 25

instruments.name: Agreement Relating to the International Telecommunications Satellite Organization (ITSO Agreement), Washington, 20 August 1971, as amended (2001 restructuring; Art. XII amendment)
instruments.note: In force 12 Feb 1973. Post-privatisation ITSO supervises public-service obligations on Common Heritage orbital/frequency assignments via a Public Services Agreement (now with SES).

instruments.name: Communications Act of 1934, 47 U.S.C. §§ 301, 308, 310 (radio station licensing, incl. space stations)
instruments.note: FCC licensing of space stations serving/controlled from the US; §310 foreign-ownership limits; basis for FCC supervision of US-licensed fleets.

instruments.name: 47 CFR Part 25 - Satellite Communications (FCC)
instruments.note: Space-station licensing rules incl. orbital-debris disclosures, GEO end-of-life disposal and 5-year post-mission LEO disposal (FCC 22-74, 2022).

instruments.name: Open-market Reorganization for the Betterment of International Telecommunications Act (ORBIT Act), Pub. L. 106-180 (2000), 47 U.S.C. § 761 et seq.
instruments.note: Set privatisation conditions for Intelsat and conditioned FCC licensing of the privatised Intelsat.

ESA.instrument: Convention for the Establishment of a European Space Agency (1975, in force 1980); ESA accepts Rescue, Liability and Registration Conventions and registers its own objects with the UN

instruments.name: Convention for the Establishment of a European Space Agency (CSE/CS(73)19, rev. 7), Paris, 30 May 1975
instruments.note: Constituent instrument; in force 30 Oct 1980. ESA has declared acceptance of the Rescue, Liability and Registration Conventions and registers ESA objects directly with UNOOSA.

instruments.name: ESA Space Debris Mitigation Requirements, ESSB-ST-U-007 Issue 1 (30 Oct 2023), under ESA Space Debris Mitigation Policy ESA/ADMIN/IPOL(2023)1
instruments.note: Internal binding requirements for ESA missions: disposal, passivation, casualty risk, collision avoidance.

instruments.name: French Law No. 2008-518 on Space Operations (for launches from the Guiana Space Centre)
instruments.note: Launches of ESA payloads from Kourou are authorised by France under the LOS (launch operator licence); ESA in-orbit operations are not LOS-authorised.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Would reach ESA assets via an EU-ESA agreement.

IT.borderline: Law 89/2025 is in force (25 June 2025) and makes space activities subject to authorisation, but the Art. 13 implementing DPCMs (requirements, file, fees, insurance bands) were not found adopted as of Sept 2026.
IT.instrument: Law No. 89 of 13 June 2025 on the space economy (authorisation, supervision, registration, liability and insurance), implementing decrees pending; Law No. 7/2018 governance; ASI registry

instruments.name: Law No. 89 of 13 June 2025, Provisions on the space economy (GU Serie Generale n. 144 of 24 June 2025)
instruments.note: Authorisation by Presidency of the Council (ASI technical authority); supervision; national registry (Arts 15-17); liability, €100m insurance (Art 21). In force 25 Jun 2025; operation awaits DPCMs.

instruments.name: Decree-Law No. 156 of 29 October 2025 (urgent economic measures), converted by Law No. 191 of 18 December 2025, Art. 3-bis
instruments.note: Amends Art. 21 of Law 89/2025 on the insurance/financial guarantee obligation of authorised space operators (insurer's liability to third parties).

instruments.name: Law No. 153 of 12 July 2005, Accession to the Convention on Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space
instruments.note: Art. 3(1) establishes the National Registry at ASI; Art. 3(2)-(6) repealed by Law 89/2025 Art. 29, which now governs registration.

instruments.name: Law No. 7 of 11 January 2018, Measures for the coordination of space and aerospace policy and provisions on the organisation and functioning of the Italian Space Agency
instruments.note: Places space policy under the Prime Minister and creates COMINT; framework within which Law 89/2025 assigns authorising and supervisory roles.

instruments.name: Legislative Decree No. 128 of 4 June 2003, Reorganisation of the Italian Space Agency (ASI)
instruments.note: ASI statute; amended 2025 by Law 89/2025 (ASI as sole technical regulator, Art. 14).

instruments.name: Law No. 23 of 25 January 1983 implementing the Liability Convention
instruments.note: Repealed by Art. 29(1) of Law 89/2025; claims for damage by foreign launching States now under Art. 20 of Law 89/2025.

instruments.name: Implementing decrees of the President of the Council of Ministers under Art. 13 of Law No. 89/2025
instruments.note: To set safety/sustainability requirements, application file, fees, sanctions, insurance risk bands and space-data rules; not found adopted as of Sept 2026 (none by March 2026).

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Coordination with Law 89/2025 pending.

considered_not_relevant.name: Decree-Law No. 21/2012 (golden power)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Investment screening; Law 89/2025 Art. 28 preserves it but it does not authorise space activities.

considered_not_relevant.name: Electronic Communications Code (Legislative Decree No. 259/2003 as replaced by Legislative Decree No. 207/2021)
considered_not_relevant.reason: General spectrum regime; not the operative space-activity authorisation.

GER.borderline: Remote-sensing-only: SatDSiG licenses operators of high-grade Earth remote-sensing systems; no general authorisation regime for other space activities. National Weltraumgesetz still an unpublished ministry draft.
GER.instrument: Satellite Data Security Act (SatDSiG) 2007: licensing of high-grade Earth remote-sensing systems (remote-sensing-only); no general space act, Weltraumgesetz draft in inter-ministerial review

instruments.name: Satellite Data Security Act (Satellitendatensicherheitsgesetz, SatDSiG) of 23 November 2007 (BGBl. I S. 2590)
instruments.note: Remote-sensing-only: licence to operate high-grade EO systems (§3), supervision, data-dissemination approval and sensitivity checks. Last amended Art. 5 Act of 19 Apr 2021 (BGBl. I S. 771).

instruments.name: Satellite Data Security Ordinance (Satellitendatensicherheitsverordnung, SatDSiV) of 26 March 2008 (BGBl. I S. 508)
instruments.note: Implements SatDSiG sensitivity check (data thresholds, ground-station/area/recipient lists). Last amended by Ordinance of 16 Oct 2023 (BGBl. 2023 I Nr. 278).

instruments.name: Space Tasks Transfer Act (Raumfahrtaufgabenübertragungsgesetz, RAÜG), promulgated 22 August 1998 (BGBl. I S. 2510)
instruments.note: Empowers DLR (space agency) to perform federal space administrative tasks in its own name; incl. SatDSiG authority functions delegated to DLR.

instruments.name: Telecommunications Act (Telekommunikationsgesetz, TKG) of 23 June 2021, § 95 (orbit positions and frequency use by satellites)
instruments.note: BNetzA files, coordinates and notifies German satellite systems with the ITU and transfers orbit/frequency rights, subject to availability, compatibility and public interest.

instruments.name: Draft Federal Space Act (Weltraumgesetz): Federal Government key points, BT-Drucksache 20/12775 (5 Sept 2024); BMFTR draft in inter-ministerial coordination
instruments.note: Would create general licensing, supervision, liability and debris rules. Minister Bär told the Bundestag on 24 Sept 2026 the draft is still in Ressortabstimmung; no cabinet bill.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Would add an EU authorisation regime.

considered_not_relevant.name: Foreign Trade and Payments Act (AWG) / Ordinance (AWV)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Export control and investment screening; no space-object authorisation.

considered_not_relevant.name: Act on the Federal Office for Information Security (BSIG) / NIS2 Implementation Act
considered_not_relevant.reason: General cybersecurity; not a space-activity authorisation regime.

GLOB.borderline: Code denotes a US commercial operator, not a multi-State body; kept as 'consortium' per dataset convention (Globalstar began as a Loral/Qualcomm partnership). Supervising State is the US.
GLOB.instrument: US: FCC licensing under Communications Act 1934 and 47 CFR Part 25 (Part 100 adopted 2026, not yet effective), with FCC orbital-debris rules; FAA launch licensing

instruments.name: Communications Act of 1934, as amended, 47 U.S.C. § 151 et seq. (esp. §§ 301, 303, 308-310)
instruments.note: Statutory basis for FCC licensing of US space stations (s.301 licence requirement; s.310(b) foreign-ownership limits). Globalstar Licensee LLC holds FCC space-station licences for its Big LEO/HIBLEO-4

instruments.name: 47 C.F.R. Part 25 – Satellite Communications
instruments.note: FCC space-station licensing rules incl. orbital-debris showings (s.25.114(d)(14)) and disposal (s.25.283); to sunset when Part 100 takes effect.

instruments.name: FCC Report and Order, Mitigation of Orbital Debris in the New Space Age, FCC 20-54 (IB Docket No. 18-313)
instruments.note: Adopted 23 Apr 2020: updated Part 25 debris disclosure rules (collision risk, casualty risk, manoeuvrability, ephemeris sharing).

instruments.name: FCC Second Report and Order, Space Innovation; Mitigation of Orbital Debris in the New Space Age, FCC 22-74
instruments.note: '5-year rule': LEO space stations ending missions must be disposed of within 5 years; applies to satellites launched after 29 Sep 2024.

instruments.name: FCC Report and Order and FNPRM, Space Modernization for the 21st Century, FCC 26-47 (SB Docket No. 25-306) – new 47 C.F.R. Part 100
instruments.note: Adopted 22 Jul 2026: replaces Part 25 with Part 100 (licensing 'assembly line', milestones, debris certifications). Effective date to be set by Space Bureau public notice.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Act, 51 U.S.C. ch. 509 (Commercial Space Launch Activities)
instruments.note: FAA licensing of Globalstar launches from US territory (e.g. Falcon 9 replacement launches); earlier launches were from Baikonur (Soyuz).

instruments.name: FCC Public Notice DA 26-550, Globalstar, Inc. and Amazon.com, Inc. seek consent to assignment/transfer of control of Globalstar licences (4 Jun 2026)
instruments.note: Pending FCC review of Amazon's acquisition of Globalstar licences; HSR waiting period expired 17 Jul 2026; closing expected 2027 per Globalstar.

instruments.name: Secure Space Act of 2026, S. 1962, 119th Congress (companion: Secure Space Act of 2025, H.R. 2458)
instruments.note: Would bar FCC satellite licences/market access for Covered-List entities. S.1962 passed Senate 23 Sep 2026 (engrossed); H.R.2458 passed House. Not enacted.

considered_not_relevant.name: Land Remote Sensing Policy Act (51 U.S.C. ch. 601) and 15 C.F.R. Part 960
considered_not_relevant.reason: NOAA private remote-sensing licensing; system is communications-only, no EO payload.

considered_not_relevant.name: Export control (ITAR, 22 C.F.R. Parts 120-130; EAR)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Controls technology transfer, not authorisation or supervision of the space objects.

CA.borderline: Remote-sensing-only: the RSSSA is the only in-force private authorisation regime. Other satellites are authorised only via ISED spectrum licences; launches only case-by-case under the Aeronautics Act/CARs until Bill C-28 passes. No statutory national registry.
CA.instrument: Remote Sensing Space Systems Act 2005 and Regulations (remote-sensing-only licensing); ISED space-station spectrum licensing (CPC-2-6-02); launch Act (Bill C-28) pending

instruments.name: Remote Sensing Space Systems Act (S.C. 2005, c. 45)
instruments.note: Licence required to operate a remote sensing space system (s.5); disposal plan, data controls, interruption orders, inspections. In force 5 Apr 2007; last amended 2007.

instruments.name: Remote Sensing Space Systems Regulations (SOR/2007-66)
instruments.note: Licence application content (incl. disposal/debris plan), licence conditions and records under the RSSSA.

instruments.name: Radiocommunication Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. R-2)
instruments.note: s.5 empowers the Minister (ISED) to issue spectrum licences for space stations and fix licence conditions; the practical basis for authorising all Canadian satellites.

instruments.name: CPC-2-6-02 — Procedure for the Submission of Applications for Spectrum Licences for Space Stations (Issue 7, April 2026)
instruments.note: ISED procedure for space-station spectrum licences; Issue 7 implements SMSE-005-26: debris plan, LEO disposal within 5 years of end of life with 90% success probability.

instruments.name: SMSE-005-26 — Decision on Changes to Licensing Requirements and Conditions of Licence for Space Debris Mitigation
instruments.note: Makes space debris mitigation (e.g. 5-year LEO post-mission disposal, orbital environment assessment) enforceable conditions of ISED space-station licences.

instruments.name: Canadian Aviation Regulations (SOR/96-433), ss. 602.43–602.44
instruments.note: Rocket launch provisions; with Aeronautics Act special authorisations, the interim case-by-case basis for Transport Canada launch approvals pending C-28.

instruments.name: CPC-2-6-04 — Procedure for the Submission of Applications to Approve the Use of Foreign-Licensed Satellites in Canada
instruments.note: ISED approval of foreign-licensed satellites serving Canada; market-access, not Art. VI authorisation.

instruments.name: Canadian Space Agency Act (S.C. 1990, c. 13)
instruments.note: Establishes the CSA and its policy/programme mandate; confers no licensing, registry or supervisory power over private operators.

instruments.name: Civil International Space Station Agreement Implementation Act (S.C. 1999, c. 35)
instruments.note: Implements the 1998 ISS IGA (jurisdiction over Canadian elements, cross-waiver of liability).

instruments.name: Bill C-28 (45th Parl., 1st Sess.), An Act to amend the Aeronautics Act and other Acts (Canadian Space Launch Act)
instruments.note: Would create a federal licensing regime for launch and re-entry from/into Canada. 1st reading 21 Apr 2026; 2nd reading debate from 28 Apr 2026; not yet in committee.

considered_not_relevant.name: Investment Canada Act (national security review)
considered_not_relevant.reason: General foreign-investment screening; does not authorise or supervise space objects.

considered_not_relevant.name: Export and Import Permits Act / Controlled Goods Program
considered_not_relevant.reason: Export-control regimes; not an authorisation of space activities.

SES.borderline: Commercial operator, not a State: Luxembourg authorises/registers Luxembourg-licensed satellites; US-licensed fleets (SES Americom, ex-Intelsat since July 2025) are licensed by the FCC.
SES.instrument: SES S.A. (Luxembourg): authorised under Luxembourg Law of 15 December 2020 on space activities and 1991 media-law concessions; US-licensed fleets (incl. ex-Intelsat) under FCC 47 CFR Part 25

instruments.name: Law of 15 December 2020 on space activities
instruments.note: Ministerial authorisation (Art. 5), continuing supervision (Art. 11), control of qualifying holdings (Art. 13), full operator liability & financial cover, National Registry of Space Objects (Art. 15).

instruments.name: Communications Act of 1934, 47 U.S.C. §§ 301, 308, 310 (radio station licensing, incl. space stations)
instruments.note: FCC licensing of space stations serving/controlled from the US; §310 foreign-ownership limits; basis for FCC supervision of US-licensed fleets.

instruments.name: 47 CFR Part 25 - Satellite Communications (FCC)
instruments.note: Space-station licensing rules incl. orbital-debris disclosures, GEO end-of-life disposal and 5-year post-mission LEO disposal (FCC 22-74, 2022).

instruments.name: Law of 27 July 1991 on electronic media, as amended (Art. 20 satellite-system concessions)
instruments.note: Concessions to establish/operate Luxembourg satellite systems using Luxembourg ITU frequency rights (SMC). Pre-2021 concessionaires needed a 2020-law authorisation from 31 Dec 2022.

instruments.name: Law of 15 December 2020 approving the Convention on Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space
instruments.note: Approval of the Registration Convention; Luxembourg acceded Jan 2021 and keeps a public national register (updated 6 July 2026).

instruments.name: Space Activities Act of the Netherlands (Wet ruimtevaartactiviteiten), 2007
instruments.note: Dutch licensing regime potentially applicable to SES satellites operated from the Netherlands (legacy New Skies/NSS fleet); fleet-level coverage not verified.

instruments.name: Regulation (EU) 2023/588 establishing the Union Secure Connectivity Programme for 2023-2027 (IRIS²)
instruments.note: EU programme under which SES is a SpaceRISE concession partner; does not itself authorise objects.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Would apply to SES as an EU operator.

SKOR.instrument: Space Development Promotion Act (Act No. 7538, 2005, as amended to Act No. 21916 of 2026) and Act on Compensation for Damage Caused by Space Objects (Act No. 8714, 2007); KASA Act (No. 20144, 2024)

instruments.name: Space Development Promotion Act (Act No. 7538, 2005, as amended)
instruments.note: Launch permits, preliminary and final registration of space objects, insurance and space-hazard planning. KASA is the authority since 27 May 2024. Latest: Act No. 21916 (15 Sep 2026).

instruments.name: Act on Compensation for Damage Caused by Space Objects (Act No. 8714, 2007, as amended)
instruments.note: Strict liability of launching operators, capped at KRW 200 billion, with mandatory liability insurance. Last substantive amendment Act No. 14839 (2017).

instruments.name: Space Development Promotion Act, partial amendment (Act No. 21866, promulgated 11 Aug 2026)
instruments.note: Adds batch launch permits (same vehicle and site, up to 5 years), launch safety zones, and MND authority for national-security launches. In force 12 Feb 2027.

instruments.name: Special Act on the Establishment and Operation of the Korea AeroSpace Administration (Act No. 20144, 2024)
instruments.note: Creates KASA (in force 27 May 2024). Transfers MSIT's permit and registration functions to KASA by consequential amendment.

instruments.name: Enforcement Decree of the Space Development Promotion Act
instruments.note: Detailed permit, registration and insurance procedures.

considered_not_relevant.name: Aerospace Industry Development Promotion Act
considered_not_relevant.reason: Industrial promotion. It creates no authorisation, registry or liability for space objects.

EUTE.borderline: Commercial company (ex-IGO), not a State: GEO fleet authorised and registered by France; OneWeb LEO fleet licensed and registered by the UK.
EUTE.instrument: Eutelsat S.A. (France): GEO fleet authorised under French Law No. 2008-518 (LOS); OneWeb LEO constellation licensed under UK Outer Space Act 1986; residual EUTELSAT IGO Convention

instruments.name: Law No. 2008-518 of 3 June 2008 on Space Operations (Loi relative aux opérations spatiales, LOS)
instruments.note: Prior authorisation of launches/in-orbit control from France or by French operators; CNES technical control; liability, insurance & State guarantee; Title VII space data. Amended 2022, 2023, 2026.

instruments.name: Outer Space Act 1986 (c. 38)
instruments.note: OneWeb Ltd (Eutelsat Group) satellites licensed by UK (CAA) under OSA; UK registers them. €60m standard cap; variable-limit reform announced Sept 2026.

instruments.name: Decree No. 2009-643 of 9 June 2009 on authorisations issued under Law No. 2008-518 on space operations
instruments.note: Authorisation/licence procedure (4-month decision), CNES conformity checks, financial-guarantee proof, defence review. Amended by Decree 2022-234 and Decree 2024-625 (from 1 July 2024).

instruments.name: Order of 31 March 2011 on the technical regulation under Decree No. 2009-643 (Réglementation technique, RT)
instruments.note: Binding technical rules: launch safety, casualty-risk limits, debris mitigation, end-of-life disposal. Amended by orders of 23 Feb 2022 (in force 1 Jan 2023) and 28 June 2024.

instruments.name: Order of 28 June 2024 amending the Order of 31 March 2011 on the technical regulation (NOR ECOI2413938A)
instruments.note: 2024 RT update (requests from 1 July 2024): mega-constellation disposal (P≥0.95, 2-5 yr), reusable launchers, in-orbit servicing, no intentional fragmentation; transitional relief to 2028.

instruments.name: Space Industry Act 2018 (c. 5)
instruments.note: Applies to orbital operations conducted from the UK (orbital operator licence), relevant to OneWeb control from UK; operator liability terms amended by Indemnities Act 2025.

instruments.name: Convention Establishing the European Telecommunications Satellite Organization (EUTELSAT), Paris, 15 July 1982, as amended (restructuring decided May 1999)
instruments.note: Residual EUTELSAT IGO oversees Eutelsat S.A.'s basic principles on IGO-origin frequency assignments; EUTELSAT has declared acceptance of the Liability and Registration Conventions.

instruments.name: Regulation (EU) 2023/588 establishing the Union Secure Connectivity Programme for 2023-2027 (IRIS²)
instruments.note: EU programme under which Eutelsat is a SpaceRISE concession partner; does not itself authorise objects.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Would apply to Eutelsat as an EU operator.

SPN.instrument: No licensing law in force: Royal Decree 278/1995 sets up only the national space-object registry; a draft Space Activities Law is at prior public consultation (AEE, Nov 2025)

instruments.name: Real Decreto 278/1995, de 24 de febrero, por el que se crea en España el Registro previsto en el Convenio de 12 de noviembre de 1974 (Registration Convention registry)
instruments.note: Creates the Spanish registry of space objects under the Registration Convention. It sets up no authorisation or licensing of private space activities.

instruments.name: Ley 11/2022, de 28 de junio, General de Telecomunicaciones
instruments.note: Radio spectrum use rights and ITU satellite-network filings. This is the only licensing that currently applies to Spanish satellites; it is not a space-activities authorisation.

instruments.name: Real Decreto 158/2023, de 7 de marzo, por el que se aprueba el Estatuto de la Agencia Estatal «Agencia Espacial Española»
instruments.note: Statute of the Spanish Space Agency (AEE). The AEE supports the competent departments on certifications, insurance and authorisations, but it grants no licences itself.

instruments.name: Anteproyecto de Ley de Actividades Espaciales (draft Space Activities Law)
instruments.note: Prior public consultation opened by the AEE in Nov 2025, aiming at a unified authorisation regime. No Council of Ministers approval found as of Sept 2026.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

ORB.borderline: Code denotes a US commercial operator (privately held since 2021), not a consortium; retained as 'consortium' per dataset convention. Supervising State is the US.
ORB.instrument: US: FCC licensing of the ORBCOMM Little LEO (NVNG MSS) system under the Communications Act 1934 and 47 CFR Part 25 (licensed 1994; OG2 modification DA 08-633), with FCC debris rules

instruments.name: Communications Act of 1934, as amended, 47 U.S.C. § 151 et seq. (esp. §§ 301, 303, 308-310)
instruments.note: Statutory basis for FCC licensing of US space stations (s.301 licence requirement; s.310(b) foreign-ownership limits). ORBCOMM License Corp. holds the FCC NVNG ('Little LEO') MSS system licence (first

instruments.name: 47 C.F.R. Part 25 – Satellite Communications
instruments.note: FCC space-station licensing rules incl. orbital-debris showings (s.25.114(d)(14)) and disposal (s.25.283); to sunset when Part 100 takes effect.

instruments.name: FCC Order and Authorization DA 08-633, Orbcomm License Corp. (modification for OG2 next-generation satellites and licence-term extension)
instruments.note: Bureau order (Mar 2008) authorising the OG2 replenishment satellites and extending the system licence; operative authorisation for current fleet.

instruments.name: FCC Report and Order, Mitigation of Orbital Debris in the New Space Age, FCC 20-54 (IB Docket No. 18-313)
instruments.note: Adopted 23 Apr 2020: updated Part 25 debris disclosure rules (collision risk, casualty risk, manoeuvrability, ephemeris sharing).

instruments.name: FCC Second Report and Order, Space Innovation; Mitigation of Orbital Debris in the New Space Age, FCC 22-74
instruments.note: '5-year rule': LEO space stations ending missions must be disposed of within 5 years; applies to satellites launched after 29 Sep 2024.

instruments.name: FCC Report and Order and FNPRM, Space Modernization for the 21st Century, FCC 26-47 (SB Docket No. 25-306) – new 47 C.F.R. Part 100
instruments.note: Adopted 22 Jul 2026: replaces Part 25 with Part 100 (licensing 'assembly line', milestones, debris certifications). Effective date to be set by Space Bureau public notice.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Act, 51 U.S.C. ch. 509 (Commercial Space Launch Activities)
instruments.note: FAA licensing of OG2 launches on Falcon 9 from the US (2014-2015).

instruments.name: Secure Space Act of 2026, S. 1962, 119th Congress (companion: Secure Space Act of 2025, H.R. 2458)
instruments.note: Would bar FCC satellite licences/market access for Covered-List entities. S.1962 passed Senate 23 Sep 2026 (engrossed); H.R.2458 passed House. Not enacted.

considered_not_relevant.name: Land Remote Sensing Policy Act (51 U.S.C. ch. 601) and 15 C.F.R. Part 960
considered_not_relevant.reason: NOAA private remote-sensing licensing; system is communications-only, no EO payload.

considered_not_relevant.name: Export control (ITAR, 22 C.F.R. Parts 120-130; EAR)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Controls technology transfer, not authorisation or supervision of the space objects.

AUS.instrument: Space (Launches and Returns) Act 2018 (launch/return and overseas payload permits, register, liability/insurance) with General, Insurance and HPR Rules 2019; ACMA space licensing

instruments.name: Space (Launches and Returns) Act 2018 (formerly Space Activities Act 1998; Act No. 123 of 1998 as amended)
instruments.note: Launch facility licences, launch/return permits, overseas payload permits; register of space objects; liability, insurance. Latest compilation C2024C00604 (14 Oct 2024, ART Act changes).

instruments.name: Space (Launches and Returns) (General) Rules 2019 (F2019L01118)
instruments.note: Application criteria incl. debris strategy, flight safety, suitably qualified experts. Amended 2023 (F2023L01084) and 2025 (F2025L00072); compilation F2025C00122; sunsets 1 Oct 2029.

instruments.name: Space (Launches and Returns) (Insurance) Rules 2019 (F2019L01120)
instruments.note: Insurance/financial requirements (Maximum Probable Loss basis, cap A$100m) for permits and authorisations; unamended since made; sunsets 1 Oct 2029.

instruments.name: Space (Launches and Returns) Legislation Amendment (Regulatory Reform) Rules 2024 (F2025L00072)
instruments.note: Made 30 Jan 2025; streamlined permit processes in the General Rules (in force from 4 Feb 2025). Spent amending instrument, automatically repealed; amendments remain in force.

instruments.name: Space (Launches and Returns) (High Power Rocket) Rules 2019 (F2019L01119)
instruments.note: Permits for high power rocket launches (sub-orbital, below 100 km).

instruments.name: Radiocommunications Act 1992
instruments.note: ACMA apparatus licensing (space and space receive licences) for Australian satellites and earth stations; ITU filings.

instruments.name: Radiocommunications (Australian Space Objects) Determination 2025 (F2025L00259)
instruments.note: ACMA determination of the Australian space objects/ITU filings on which apparatus-licensed operation depends; in force 3 Mar 2025, replacing the 2014 Determination.

instruments.name: Radiocommunications (Foreign Space Objects) Determination 2025 (F2025L00260)
instruments.note: Lists foreign space objects that Australian-licensed earth stations may communicate with; replaced the 2014 Determination.

instruments.name: Radiocommunications (Communication with Space Object) Class Licence 2025 (F2025L00261)
instruments.note: Class licence for user terminals communicating with space objects; replaced the 2015 class licence.

considered_not_relevant.name: Space (Launches and Returns) Legislation Amendment (Suitably Qualified Experts) Rules 2023 (F2023L01084)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Spent amending instrument (Aug 2023); its changes are incorporated in the General Rules compilation.

considered_not_relevant.name: Australian Space Agency
considered_not_relevant.reason: Created administratively in 2018 within the Department of Industry; no establishing statute (the Act's regulator functions sit with the Minister/delegates).

TURK.instrument: No space activities licensing law. Turkish Space Agency set up by Presidential Decree No. 23 (OG 30624, 13 Dec 2018). Satellite communications authorised under Electronic Communications Law No. 5809

instruments.name: Presidential Decree No. 23 on the Turkish Space Agency (Official Gazette No. 30624, 13 December 2018)
instruments.note: Creates TUA and gives it policy, coordination and drafting functions. No licensing procedure for space activities has been issued under it.

instruments.name: Electronic Communications Law No. 5809 (2008)
instruments.note: BTK authorisation of satellite communications services and frequency use. Telecoms only.

instruments.name: Draft Law on the Establishment of the Turkish Space Agency and Regulation of Space Activities (1/823)
instruments.note: Government bill submitted 24 Feb 2017. Superseded by Decree No. 23 (2018). No 2025-26 space activities bill found in TBMM records (search limited).

ARGN.borderline: CONAE has sole competence over the national space programme under Decree 995/91, and a registry exists (Decree 125/95). No statute or decree creates a licensing regime for non-governmental operators. A comprehensive bill is pending (March 2026).
ARGN.instrument: No space activities licensing law; CONAE created by Decree No. 995/1991; National Registry of Objects Launched into Outer Space (Decree No. 125/1995); 2026 'Ley Espacial Argentina' bill pending

instruments.name: Decree No. 125/1995 (National Registry of Objects Launched into Outer Space)
instruments.note: Creates the national registry under CONAE for Registration Convention purposes (B.O. 25 Jul 1995).

instruments.name: Decree No. 995/1991 (creation of the Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales – CONAE)
instruments.note: CONAE as sole State body for the space programme and for proposing export controls on space technology. No private licensing; later decrees (e.g. 901/2025) only change its board.

instruments.name: Law No. 24,158 (approval of the Convention on Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space)
instruments.note: Parliamentary approval of the Registration Convention.

instruments.name: Law No. 27,078 (Argentina Digital – ICT law) with DNU No. 267/2015 (ENACOM)
instruments.note: Spectrum and satellite-service authorisation by ENACOM; telecom only.

instruments.name: Law No. 26,092 (creation of AR-SAT; authorisation to use 81°W orbital position)
instruments.note: Creates the State satellite operator and allocates the orbital position; State-owned operations, not a private authorisation regime.

instruments.name: Bill 'Ley Espacial Argentina – Régimen Nacional de Actividades Espaciales' (Chamber of Deputies, Dep. M. M. Pagano, March 2026)
instruments.note: Would create DINAEC within CONAE to license and supervise commercial space activities, with liability and financial-coverage rules. Not debated; expediente no. not verified.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law No. 27,208 (Argentine Geostationary Satellite Plan 2015-2035)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Industrial-policy statute for AR-SAT; no authorisation or supervision regime.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law No. 26,306 (meteorites cultural heritage registry)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Concerns meteorites on Argentine territory, not space objects.

ROC.instrument: Space Development Act (promulgated 16 Jun 2021, in force 20 Jan 2022, amended 28 Jun 2023) with 2022 registration and launch-permit regulations

instruments.name: Space Development Act
instruments.note: Registration of launch vehicles and spacecraft (incl. ROC entities launching abroad), launch permits, liability and insurance. In force 20 Jan 2022. 2023 amendment added penalties.

instruments.name: Regulations for Registration of Launch Vehicle and Spacecraft
instruments.note: Made under Art. 10. Registration includes a type safety review, and applies to foreign registrants launching from Taiwan and ROC nationals launching abroad. Issued 18 Jan 2022.

instruments.name: Regulations Governing Launch Permits for Launch Vehicles and Handling of Space Accidents (發射載具發射許可及太空事故處理辦法)
instruments.note: Made under Arts. 11 and 15. Covers launch permit applications, refusal grounds and accident handling. Issued 18 Jan 2022.

instruments.name: Regulations for Provision and Compensation for Information Obtained by Private Sector with Spacecraft
instruments.note: Government may order private spacecraft data holders to supply data in emergencies, with compensation. Not an operator licence.

instruments.name: Act for the Establishment of the Taiwan Space Agency
instruments.note: TASA is entrusted with reviewing registrations and launch permits. Promulgated 4 May 2022.

O3B.state: O3b / O3b mPOWER (SES group; UK-licensed and UK-registered)
O3B.borderline: Commercial operator in a multinational group (SES, Luxembourg), not a multi-State body; retained as 'consortium'. Licensing and registration State is the UK (via OSA and its Jersey extension).
O3B.instrument: UK: Outer Space Act 1986 licences (extended to Jersey by S.I. 1990/597) and UK registration; ownership moved to Astra (GB) Ltd, London, Apr 2025. Luxembourg (SES parent) does not license these satellites

instruments.name: Outer Space Act 1986 (c. 38)
instruments.note: All O3b (M001-M020) and O3b mPOWER (MP01-MP10) satellites hold OSA licences (e.g. 3 May 2013; 9 Dec 2022) and are on the UK Register.

instruments.name: Outer Space Act 1986 (Jersey) Order 1990 (S.I. 1990/597)
instruments.note: Extends the OSA to Jersey; licensee O3b Limited is a Jersey company (St Helier) per the UK Register.

instruments.name: UK Register of Space Objects (CAP 2207) and UK Supplementary Register (CAP 2208), Civil Aviation Authority
instruments.note: UK Register (Aug 2026) lists O3b M001-M020 and MP01-MP10, owner O3b Ltd (Jersey); 'ownership transferred in April 2025 to Astra (GB) limited', London.

instruments.name: Space Industry Act 2018 (c. 5)
instruments.note: Licensing of spaceflight activities carried out in the UK incl. orbital operations from UK (in force for licensing 29 Jul 2021); s.61 register; s.34-36 liability/indemnity.

instruments.name: Space Industry Regulations 2021 (S.I. 2021/792)
instruments.note: Implementing regulations for SIA 2018 licences (orbital operator licence conditions, safety, insurance); in force 29 Jul 2021.

instruments.name: Deregulation Act 2015 (c. 20), s. 12
instruments.note: Amended OSA 1986 s.10 so licences may (and in practice do) limit the licensee's indemnity to the Government.

instruments.name: Space Industry (Indemnities) Act 2025 (c. 35)
instruments.note: Royal Assent 18 Dec 2025, in force Feb 2026: amends SIA 2018 ss.12(2), 36(3) so every operator licence must specify the licensee's indemnity limit.

instruments.name: Law of 15 December 2020 on space activities (Luxembourg)
instruments.note: Luxembourg regime for operators with seat in Luxembourg (SES S.A. parent); O3b satellites are licensed and registered by the UK, not Luxembourg.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final
instruments.note: Commission proposal (June 2025) for EU-wide authorisation, registration and safety/debris rules, incl. for third-country operators serving the EU; in legislative procedure.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law of 20 July 2017 on the exploration and use of space resources (Luxembourg)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Space-resources missions only; irrelevant to O3b communications satellites.

FIN.instrument: Act on Space Activities (63/2018), amended by Act 97/2023 (adds satellite remote-sensing licensing), with MEAE Decree 74/2018 and Government Decree 892/2023

instruments.name: Laki avaruustoiminnasta 63/2018 (Act on Space Activities)
instruments.note: Authorisation by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment, supervision, national registry, operator liability, insurance and State recourse, debris mitigation. In force 23 Jan 2018.

instruments.name: Laki avaruustoiminnasta annetun lain muuttamisesta 97/2023 (Act amending the Act on Space Activities)
instruments.note: In force 1 Feb 2023. Adds a new chapter 2a licensing satellite remote sensing above set performance thresholds, and security considerations.

instruments.name: Työ- ja elinkeinoministeriön asetus avaruustoiminnasta 74/2018 (Decree of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment on Space Activities)
instruments.note: Detailed authorisation application content and registry of space objects.

instruments.name: Valtioneuvoston asetus satelliittikaukokartoitusta koskevista raja-arvoista 892/2023 (Government Decree on satellite remote-sensing threshold values)
instruments.note: Sets the performance thresholds that trigger remote-sensing licensing under Act 63/2018 as amended.

instruments.name: Laki maa-asemista ja eräistä tutkista 96/2023 (Act on Ground Stations and Certain Radars)
instruments.note: In force 1 Feb 2023. Registration and security screening of ground stations and space-surveillance radars operating in Finland.

instruments.name: Laki sähköisen viestinnän palveluista 917/2014 (Act on Electronic Communications Services)
instruments.note: Radio licences and satellite frequency filings (Traficom).

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

NOR.instrument: Space Act (Act of 22 December 2025 No. 128), in force 1 July 2026, replacing Act No. 38 of 1969; Civil Aviation Authority designated supervisor; satellite regulations still in draft

instruments.name: Lov 22. desember 2025 nr. 128 om aktiviteter i verdensrommet (romloven) (Space Act)
instruments.note: Framework act (8 chapters, 29 sections) covering permits, transfers, registration, operator duties, compensation and insurance, supervision and enforcement. In force 1 Jul 2026.

instruments.name: Forskrift 30. juni 2026 nr. 1450 om tilsynsmyndighet etter romloven (FOR-2026-06-30-1450)
instruments.note: Designates Luftfartstilsynet (Civil Aviation Authority) as supervisory authority under the Space Act. In force 1 Jul 2026.

instruments.name: Lov 13. desember 2024 nr. 76 om elektronisk kommunikasjon (ekomloven)
instruments.note: Frequency authorisation and ITU filings for satellite networks (Nkom). Amended alongside the Space Act.

instruments.name: Draft regulation on satellites and other space objects under the Space Act (forskrift, public consultation planned autumn 2026)
instruments.note: Implementing rules for satellites, to be followed by orbital launch (2026) and spaceport and suborbital regulations (2027). Not yet consulted as of Sept 2026.

considered_not_relevant.name: Lov 13. juni 1969 nr. 38 om oppskyting av gjenstander fra norsk territorium m.m. ut i verdensrommet
considered_not_relevant.reason: Repealed from 1 Jul 2026 by the Space Act 2025

ISRA.instrument: No space legislation. Israeli Space Law (licensing, supervision, liability) in advanced inter-ministerial drafting (LSC 2026). Satellite communications licensed under the Communications Law 1982

instruments.name: Communications (Telecommunications and Broadcasting) Law, 5742-1982
instruments.note: Ministry of Communications licensing of satellite communications services and frequencies. Telecoms only. No official English online text verified.

instruments.name: Israeli Space Law (draft)
instruments.note: In advanced inter-ministerial drafting per Israel's LSC 2026 statement. It will set licensing, supervision and liability. Not yet before the Knesset.

considered_not_relevant.name: Defense Export Control Law, 5766-2007
considered_not_relevant.reason: Export control. It does not authorise or supervise space objects.

BRAZ.borderline: Law 14,946/2024 requires the AEB and Air Force to update their regulations within 365 days (Art. 47). No post-2024 AEB regulation was found, so licensing still runs under REB Parts 1–3 (2021–2022).
BRAZ.instrument: Law No. 14,946/2024 (national space activities: AEB/COMAER authorisation, RESBRA registry, guarantees/insurance, debris) with AEB Brazilian Space Regulations (REB) Parts 1–3

instruments.name: Law No. 14,946 of 31 July 2024 (Institui normas aplicáveis a atividades espaciais nacionais)
instruments.note: AEB authorises civil and COMAER defence activities; RESBRA registry (Art.25); guarantees/insurance; debris (Art.35). In force 1 Aug 2024; veto overridden, promulgated 1 Jul 2025.

instruments.name: AEB Portaria No. 698 of 31 August 2021 — Brazilian Space Regulation (REB) Parts 1 (Operator Licence) and 2 (Launch Authorisation)
instruments.note: Licensing of launch operators (5-yr licence) and launch authorisation from Brazil; revoked Portarias AEB 5/2002, 160/2009, 3/2011 and 182/2020.

instruments.name: AEB Portaria No. 1,019 of 23 December 2022 — Brazilian Space Regulation (REB) Part 3 (Insurance Requirements for Space Launch)
instruments.note: Sets insurance requirements for launches authorised by the AEB.

instruments.name: AEB Portaria No. 96 of 30 November 2011 (Registration of Space Objects)
instruments.note: Sets up Brazil's national register of space objects for the Registration Convention; to be superseded by RESBRA under Law 14,946 (Art. 25).

instruments.name: Law No. 8,854 of 10 February 1994 (creates the Brazilian Space Agency – AEB)
instruments.note: Creates the AEB and empowers it to set norms and issue licences and authorisations for space activities; the legal basis for REB before 2024.

instruments.name: AEB Resolution No. 54 of 10 July 2001 (SINCESPAÇO – National Certification System in the Space Area)
instruments.note: Certification system for quality and safety of space products and activities.

instruments.name: Decree No. 1,953 of 10 July 1996 (National System for the Development of Space Activities – SINDAE)
instruments.note: Organises SINDAE with the AEB as its central body; confers no licensing power.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law No. 9,994/2000 (Space Science and Technology Development Programme funding)
considered_not_relevant.reason: R&D funding; no authorisation, registry or liability function.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law No. 9,472/1997 (General Telecommunications Law) / ANATEL satellite rules
considered_not_relevant.reason: Satellite exploitation rights and spectrum; relevant only to telecom, not the space-activity authorisation under Law 14,946.

UAE.instrument: Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2023 on the Regulation of the Space Sector, with Cabinet Resolution No. 203 of 2025 (authorisations), Cabinet Resolution No. 20 of 2023 (liability guarantee) and UAESA registration rules

instruments.name: Federal Decree-Law No. (46) of 2023 Concerning the Regulation of the Space Sector
instruments.note: Replaced Federal Law No. 12 of 2019. UAESA permit required for all space activities; registry, debris duties, liability. UAESA 90-day compliance grace period from 27 Jul 2026.

instruments.name: Cabinet Resolution No. (203) of 2025 Regarding the Regulations on the Authorizations of Space Activities and Other Space Sector Related Activities
instruments.note: Implementing authorisation regime under Decree-Law 46/2023 (operations, launch incl. sounding rockets, re-entry sites, launch facilities); replaces Cabinet Resolution No. 18 of 2023.

instruments.name: Cabinet Resolution No. (20) of 2023 on the Regulations Ensuring Compensation for Damage Caused to Third Parties during the Exercise of Space Activities and Other Space Sector Related Activities
instruments.note: Operator guarantee/insurance set by UAESA per risk; operator liable up to compensation limit; State recourse beyond it. Adopted under Law 12/2019; continuation under Decree-Law 46/2023 assumed.

instruments.name: UAE Space Agency Regulation on the Registration of Space Objects (2022)
instruments.note: Issued 23 Aug 2022, effective 60 days after Official Gazette publication; replaced Board Decision 9/5/2017. National registry feeding UN registration. Post-2023 status not independently confirmed.

instruments.name: UAE Space Agency Regulation on Human Spaceflight Activities (2022)
instruments.note: Conditions for authorised human spaceflight activities; issued under Federal Law 12/2019.

instruments.name: Cabinet Resolution No. (19) of 2023 Concerning the Space Resources Regulations
instruments.note: Authorisation and conditions for exploration/exploitation of space resources.

instruments.name: UAE Space Agency Space Debris Mitigation Guidelines (2022)
instruments.note: Guidelines applied to operators through permit conditions; Decree-Law 46/2023 requires debris mitigation plans and reporting of debris.
