instruments.name: Federal Law by Decree No. (3) of 2003 Regarding the Organization of the Telecommunications Sector (as amended)
instruments.note: TDRA manages spectrum and orbital resources and ITU filings for UAE satellites.

instruments.name: Federal Law No. (12) of 2019 on the Regulation of the Space Sector
instruments.note: First UAE space law; repealed and replaced by Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2023.

considered_not_relevant.name: Cabinet Resolution No. (21) of 2023 (administrative penalties, space sector)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Penalty schedule only; not separately verified as still in force after Decree-Law 46/2023, and adds no authorisation, registry or liability function.

INDO.instrument: Law No. 21 of 2013 on Space Activities (licensing, registration, liability, insurance), implemented by GR 11/2018 (remote sensing), GR 7/2023 (space technology) and GR 22/2026 (spaceports)

instruments.name: Law of the Republic of Indonesia No. 21 of 2013 on Space Activities (Undang-Undang Nomor 21 Tahun 2013 tentang Keantariksaan), LN 2013 No. 133
instruments.note: Framework act: activity and launch permits (izin kegiatan/peluncuran), space-object registration, liability, compulsory 3rd-party insurance, debris mitigation; licence revocation (Art 94).

instruments.name: Government Regulation No. 22 of 2026 on the Administration of Spaceports (Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 22 Tahun 2026 tentang Penyelenggaraan Bandar Antariksa)
instruments.note: In force 12 May 2026 under Law 21/2013: spaceport-operator licence from the Agency (BRIN), launch-vehicle operator licensing, liability, compulsory 3rd-party insurance (Art 58), supervision.

instruments.name: Government Regulation No. 11 of 2018 on Procedures for Conducting Remote Sensing Activities (Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 11 Tahun 2018 tentang Tata Cara Penyelenggaraan Kegiatan Penginderaan Jauh)
instruments.note: Implements Art 23 of Law 21/2013: remote-sensing data acquisition, processing and distribution regime incl. licences and administrative sanctions (suspension/revocation).

instruments.name: Government Regulation No. 7 of 2023 on Mastery of Space Technology (Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 7 Tahun 2023 tentang Penguasaan Teknologi Keantariksaan), LN 2023 No. 26
instruments.note: Implements Law 21/2013 (16 Feb 2023): Agency permits for rocket-motor development and static/flight tests, licensing of sensitive space-technology imports, safety and security standards.

instruments.name: Regulation of the Minister of Communication and Digital Affairs No. 3 of 2025 on the Use of Radio Frequency Spectrum for Satellite Services and Satellite Orbits
instruments.note: March 2025; repeals Permenkominfo 21/2014. Satellite filings, space/earth station spectrum licences, landing rights for foreign satellites, end-of-life de-orbit duty (Art 74), sanctions.

instruments.name: Presidential Regulation No. 45 of 2017 on the Master Plan for Space Activities 2016-2040 (Peraturan Presiden Nomor 45 Tahun 2017 tentang Rencana Induk Penyelenggaraan Keantariksaan Tahun 2016-2040)
instruments.note: Master plan under Law 21/2013 (programmatic; no licensing provisions).

instruments.name: Presidential Regulation No. 78 of 2021 on the National Research and Innovation Agency (Peraturan Presiden Nomor 78 Tahun 2021 tentang Badan Riset dan Inovasi Nasional)
instruments.note: BRIN absorbed LAPAN and exercises the space-agency ('Badan') functions under Law 21/2013, incl. licensing and registration.

instruments.name: Law No. 21 of 2025 on Airspace Management (Undang-Undang Nomor 21 Tahun 2025 tentang Pengelolaan Ruang Udara)
instruments.note: Enacted 24 Dec 2025: fixes the upper limit of national airspace at 110 km; regulates the 'subantariksa' zone and operators' third-party liability there.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law No. 11 of 2020 on Job Creation / Perppu 2/2022 as enacted by Law No. 6 of 2023
considered_not_relevant.reason: No evidence that it amended Law 21/2013: consolidated status on pasal.id shows Law 21/2013 unamended and in force, and a keyword search of the Job Creation text returns no 'keantariksaan' amendment. The full annex text could not be retrieved to confirm.

considered_not_relevant.name: Government Regulation No. 28 of 2025 on Risk-Based Business Licensing
considered_not_relevant.reason: General OSS business-licensing framework; not found to create a space-specific authorisation. Not verified in full text.

IM.borderline: Former intergovernmental organisation now a private UK company; retained as 'consortium'. Operative supervising State is the UK.
IM.instrument: UK: Outer Space Act 1986 licences (plus Isle of Man extension) and UK registration; SIA 2018 for newer licences; IMSO Convention (as amended 1998/2008) governs residual public-service oversight

instruments.name: Outer Space Act 1986 (c. 38)
instruments.note: Inmarsat-4, -5, GX5 and -6 satellites licensed under OSA (e.g. I-6 F1 16 Dec 2021) and on UK Register; IGO-era I-2/I-3 licensed 23 Mar 1999 (Supplementary Register).

instruments.name: Space Industry Act 2018 (c. 5)
instruments.note: Inmarsat-6 F2 (2023-022A) licensed under both OSA 1986 and SIA 2018 (13 Feb 2023) per UK Register.

instruments.name: Outer Space Act 1986 (Isle of Man) Order 1990 (S.I. 1990/596), as amended by S.I. 2019/258
instruments.note: Extends the OSA to the Isle of Man; Inmarsat Launch Company Ltd (Douglas, IoM) is co-owner of Inmarsat 5-F3 on the UK Register.

instruments.name: UK Register of Space Objects (CAP 2207) and UK Supplementary Register (CAP 2208), Civil Aviation Authority
instruments.note: UK Register lists I-4 F1-F3, I-5 F1-F4, GX5, I-6 F1-F2; Supplementary Register (CAP 2208) lists IGO-era I2-F1..F4 and I3 satellites.

instruments.name: Space Industry Regulations 2021 (S.I. 2021/792)
instruments.note: Implementing regulations for SIA 2018 licences (orbital operator licence conditions, safety, insurance); in force 29 Jul 2021.

instruments.name: Deregulation Act 2015 (c. 20), s. 12
instruments.note: Amended OSA 1986 s.10 so licences may (and in practice do) limit the licensee's indemnity to the Government.

instruments.name: Space Industry (Indemnities) Act 2025 (c. 35)
instruments.note: Royal Assent 18 Dec 2025, in force Feb 2026: amends SIA 2018 ss.12(2), 36(3) so every operator licence must specify the licensee's indemnity limit.

instruments.name: Convention on the International Mobile Satellite Organization (IMSO), 1976, as amended 1998 (in force 31 Jul 2001) and 2008
instruments.note: Constituent instrument of former IGO; since privatisation IMSO oversees GMDSS/LRIT public-service obligations, not licensing or registration.

considered_not_relevant.name: US Communications Act / FCC market-access grants for Inmarsat
considered_not_relevant.reason: FCC grants US market access to UK-licensed satellites; does not authorise or supervise the space objects (Viasat ownership does not change licensing State).

SING.instrument: No space act. Non-binding 2024 Guidelines for Singapore-Related Space Activities (updated 2026) and a registry; IMDA orbital-slot licences (Telecommunications Act 1999); NSAS (from 1 Apr 2026) to draft law

instruments.name: Telecommunications Act 1999 (2020 Revised Edition)
instruments.note: Basis for IMDA's 'Licence for the Use of Satellite Orbital Slot' and management of Singapore's ITU satellite filings. Spectrum/orbit licensing only; not an Art VI regime.

instruments.name: IMDA Satellite Filing Requirements and Guidelines: Licence for the Use of Satellite Orbital Slot (last updated 19 April 2026)
instruments.note: IMDA assesses satellite-operator filing requests under the ITU Radio Regulations and issues orbital-slot licences.

instruments.name: Guidelines for Singapore-Related Space Activities (OSTIn, May 2024; updated 24 March 2026 by NSAS)
instruments.note: Non-binding guidelines ('should comply'); request registration in the NSAS national registry at least 30 days before launch. No licensing.

considered_not_relevant.name: Establishment of the National Space Agency of Singapore (1 April 2026)
considered_not_relevant.reason: NSAS was set up within MTI by administrative decision, not by a statute that confers authorising powers. Its mandate includes enacting space legislation. No space bill was found in Parliament; officials have indicated legislation in 3 to 5 years.

AB.borderline: No national authorisation instrument verified for Arabsat satellites; responsibility rests with member States collectively (OST Art. VI/XIII). Saudi (host State) space instruments could not be verified (CST site JS-only).
AB.instrument: Intergovernmental organisation under the Agreement of the Arab Corporation for Space Communications (Cairo, 1976, amended 1990), HQ Riyadh; no Art. VII Registration Convention declaration

instruments.name: Agreement of the Arab Corporation for Space Communications (ARABSAT), Cairo, 14 Apr 1976 (in force 16 Jul 1976; amended May 1990)
instruments.note: Constituent treaty of the Arab League satellite IGO (depositary: League of Arab States); governs ownership and operation of Arabsat satellites.

GREC.instrument: Law 4508/2017 on authorisation of space activities, national registry of space objects and the Greek space organisation, as amended by Law 4712/2020

instruments.name: Νόμος 4508/2017 (ΦΕΚ Α' 200/22.12.2017) Authorisation of space activities – Registration in the National Register of Space Objects – Establishment of a Greek Space Organisation
instruments.note: Ministerial authorisation with debris-mitigation and non-contamination conditions, environmental reporting, national registry, liability and insurance. Amended by Law 4712/2020.

instruments.name: Νόμος 4712/2020 (ΦΕΚ Α' 146/29.07.2020), amending Law 4508/2017
instruments.note: Amends the 2017 space law, including the licensing provisions reported to UNOOSA for debris mitigation.

instruments.name: Νόμος 4623/2019 (ΦΕΚ Α' 134/09.08.2019), Article 60: establishment of the Hellenic Space Center
instruments.note: Creates the Hellenic Space Center (ELKE). It succeeded the Hellenic Space Organisation S.A. created by Art. 18 of Law 4508/2017, which was abolished.

instruments.name: Νόμος 4727/2020 (Digital governance and Electronic Communications Code)
instruments.note: Radio spectrum licensing and satellite filings by EETT.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

SAUD.borderline: CST Ordinance as amended by CoM Res. 430 (2024/25) lets CST license the space sector, and CST registers telecom space stations, but no space-activities licensing law or regulation is in force; CST rules still draft
SAUD.instrument: No space law in force: draft Space Law and implementing regulations (per KSA, LSC Apr 2026); CST 'Space Sector Regulations and Guidelines' consulted Dec 2025–Mar 2026, not adopted; CST Ordinance and NTN rules apply

instruments.name: Ordinance of the Communications, Space and Technology Commission (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 74 of 5/3/1422H), as amended by Resolutions No. 253 of 7/4/1444H and No. 430 of 23/6/1446H
instruments.note: Res. 253 (2022) moved civil space regulation to CST; Res. 430 (Official Gazette 17 Jan 2025) empowers CST to issue licences/permits and keep national registers. Framework only.

instruments.name: CST Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) Regulations, incl. Regulation for Registration of Telecommunication Space Stations
instruments.note: Published 20 Sep 2022; space stations serving KSA must register in CST Space Station Registry. Telecom market access, not Art VI authorisation. Update consulted Oct 2025.

instruments.name: Ordinance of the Saudi Space Agency (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 821 of 24/11/1444H)
instruments.note: SSA (ex-Saudi Space Commission) statute: strategy, programmes, research; regulatory role lies with CST.

instruments.name: CST Space Sector Regulations and Guidelines (draft for public consultation)
instruments.note: Consultation 25 Dec 2025–24 Mar 2026: licensing of space object ops, launch, spaceports, resources, SST, national registry, insurance. No adoption found by 24 Sep 2026.

instruments.name: Draft Space Law of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its implementing regulations
instruments.note: Reported as drafted by KSA at COPUOS LSC, 15–22 Apr 2026; not yet enacted by royal decree.

considered_not_relevant.name: Frequency Use Licence Remuneration (Council of Ministers Resolution 632, 2022)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Spectrum fee instrument only; no authorisation or supervision of space objects.

SWED.instrument: Act on Space Activities (1982:963) and Decree on Space Activities (1982:1069); a new Space Activities Act is at draft Law Council referral stage (Ju2026/01714), proposed in force 1 July 2027

instruments.name: Lag (1982:963) om rymdverksamhet (Act on Space Activities)
instruments.note: Government licence needed for non-State space activities from Sweden and by Swedish persons abroad. State recourse against operator (s.6). Last amended by SFS 2021:1025.

instruments.name: Förordning (1982:1069) om rymdverksamhet (Decree on Space Activities)
instruments.note: Applications go to Rymdstyrelsen, which supervises licensees and keeps the national registry of space objects for UN reporting. Amended by SFS 1994:114. UNOOSA lists it as '1982:1062' in error.

instruments.name: Förordning (2007:1115) med instruktion för Rymdstyrelsen

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)

considered_not_relevant.reason: Creates the agency but gives it no power to authorise or register private space activities. Official text not fetched.

MALA.instrument: Malaysian Space Board Act 2022 (Act 834): licensing, registration, absolute liability and insurance. Fully in force from 1 Jan 2025 together with the Malaysian Space Board Regulations 2024

instruments.name: Malaysian Space Board Act 2022 (Act 834)
instruments.note: Royal Assent 19 Jan 2022; gazetted 25 Jan 2022; fully in force 1 Jan 2025. Establishes the Board; licences (Part IV), registration (Part V), absolute liability and indemnity (Part VI).

instruments.name: Malaysian Space Board Regulations 2024
instruments.note: Made under Act 834; in force 1 Jan 2025 per Malaysia's LSC statements. Licensing detail incl. debris mitigation and flight-safety plans. P.U.(A) number not verified.

instruments.note: MCMC spectrum and apparatus assignments and network-facility licences for satellite systems and ground stations.

considered_not_relevant.name: National Space Policy 2030
considered_not_relevant.reason: Policy only. The operative basis of supervision is Act 834.

LUXE.instrument: Law of 15 December 2020 on space activities (authorisation, supervision, registry) and Law of 20 July 2017 on space resources; satellite concessions under the 1991 electronic media law

instruments.name: Law of 15 December 2020 on space activities
instruments.note: Ministerial authorisation (Art. 5), continuing supervision (Art. 11), control of qualifying holdings (Art. 13), full operator liability & financial cover, National Registry of Space Objects (Art. 15).

instruments.name: Law of 20 July 2017 on the exploration and use of space resources
instruments.note: Written mission authorisation for exploring/using space resources (Art. 2); supervision; operator liability; resources capable of appropriation (Art. 1).

instruments.note: Approval of the Registration Convention; Luxembourg acceded Jan 2021 and keeps a public national register (updated 6 July 2026).

instruments.note: Concessions to establish/operate Luxembourg satellite systems using Luxembourg ITU frequency rights (SMC). Pre-2021 concessionaires needed a 2020-law authorisation from 31 Dec 2022.

instruments.name: Law of 17 December 2021 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/1972 (European Electronic Communications Code)
instruments.note: General electronic-communications and spectrum regime (ILR) applying to satellite-based networks and services.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Pending: Council compromise text Dec 2025; EP ITRE draft Mar 2026, vote awaited. Would overlay the 2020 law.

considered_not_relevant.name: Luxembourg Space Agency (LSA)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Promotional agency without a founding statute conferring authorising or registry powers; the Minister of the Economy authorises and registers.

PAKI.borderline: The Rules are binding secondary legislation (S.R.O. in the Gazette Extraordinary, in force immediately) made by the NCA under the National Command Authority Act 2010, not a dedicated space statute. PAKI.instrument: Pakistan Space Activities Rules 2024 (S.R.O. 60(I)/2024, Gazette 2 Feb 2024) under the National Command Authority Act 2010: PSARB authorisation, registration, supervision, insurance and remote-sensing permits

instruments.name: Pakistan Space Activities Rules, 2024 (S.R.O. 60(I)/2024)
instruments.note: Notified 1 Feb 2024, Gazette Extra. Pt II 2 Feb 2024, in force immediately. Creates PSARB; no space object without its authorisation (r.11); insurance; RS permits (r.20).

instruments.name: National Command Authority Act, 2010 (Act V of 2010)
instruments.note: Enabling Act: the Rules were made under s.15 read with ss.3(6) and 7(a), with Federal Government approval. Cited in the S.R.O. preamble; standalone official text not fetched.

instruments.name: Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission Ordinance, 1981 (XX of 1981)
instruments.note: Constitutes SUPARCO as the National Space Agency, which also serves as the PSARB secretariat under the 2024 Rules. Cited in the Rules; text not fetched.

instruments.name: National Space Policy of Pakistan (13 December 2023)
instruments.note: Policy calling for space laws and regulatory frameworks. Not itself binding.

considered_not_relevant.name: Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996
considered_not_relevant.reason: Governs telecom and spectrum through the PTA and the Frequency Allocation Board. Satellite authorisation now sits with PSARB under the 2024 Rules.

IRAN.borderline: The Statute of the Iranian Space Agency (Cabinet, 2005, under Art. 9 of the 2003 ICT Ministry Law) lists 'issuing the authorization for space activities' among ISA's tasks. But no published authorisation regime (procedure, conditions) was found, and the statute is an agency-creation instrument. Hence 'no'.

instruments.name: Statute of the Iranian Space Agency (Cabinet resolution of 11 June 2005)
instruments.note: Art. 3(VIII): ISA issues authorisations for space activities under Supreme Space Council approvals. Art. 3(XII): orbital slots and registration. Text is an unofficial translation (J. Space Law).

instruments.name: Law on the Duties and Powers of the Ministry of Information and Communications Technology (10 December 2003), Art. 9
instruments.note: Statutory basis for ISA and the Supreme Space Council. Majlis Research Center record not retrievable (503).

MEX.borderline: The 2025 telecom law gives the CRT concessions over orbital resources and makes deorbiting a GSO satellite subject to CRT authorisation (Art. 140). Under the rule this is telecom/spectrum licensing, not a space-activity authorisation regime.
MEX.instrument: No space-activities licensing law; Ley que Crea la Agencia Espacial Mexicana (DOF 30 Jul 2010); satellites via orbital-resource concessions under the Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (DOF 16 Jul 2025)

instruments.name: Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (DOF 16 July 2025)
instruments.note: Repealed the 2014 LFTR. CRT grants orbital-resource concessions (up to 20 yrs) and foreign-satellite authorisations. Arts 136–142: relocation/deorbit authorisation, contingency plans.

instruments.name: Ley que Crea la Agencia Espacial Mexicana (DOF 30 July 2010)
instruments.note: Creates the AEM with policy and coordination functions; no licensing or registry power. Unamended since 2010.

instruments.name: Programa Espacial Mexicano 2026-2030 (DOF)
instruments.note: Sectoral programme for space; policy only, not a legal basis for authorisation.

instruments.name: Constitutional reform of Arts. 28 and 73 on outer-space activities (minuta)
instruments.note: Would declare space activities a priority area and let Congress legislate on them, a prerequisite for a national space law. Passed Deputies 2023; still pending in the Senate in 2026.

considered_not_relevant.name: Ley Federal de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (2014)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Abrogated by the 2025 Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión.

instruments.name: Arrêté royal du 15 mars 2022 portant exécution de certaines dispositions de la loi du 17 septembre 2005 (Royal Decree of 15 March 2022)

instruments.note: Delegates the minister's powers under the Outer Space Act to the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science, which acts as licensing and registry authority.

instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

instruments.note: FAA/AST licensed every Sea Launch mission (1999-2014) as a US-licensed commercial launch operator; third-party liability insurance and US indemnification regime.

instruments.name: 14 C.F.R. Part 450 – Launch and Reentry License Requirements
instruments.note: FAA streamlined launch/reentry licensing rule (in force 10 Mar 2021; legacy licences transitioned by 10 Mar 2026).

considered_not_relevant.name: Norwegian and Ukrainian/Russian space legislation
considered_not_relevant.reason: Partners' States did not license the sea launches; operations from the high seas under US licence. No launches since 2014; assets sold to S7 Group (2016-18).

NICO.state: New ICO / ICO Global Communications (ICO F2, now Omnispace OMNI-M1)
NICO.borderline: Commercial operator code (ex-ICO, now Omnispace, US) with one object; retained as 'consortium'. Supervising and registering State: US.
NICO.instrument: Sole object ICO F2 (2001-026A), launched from Cape Canaveral and registered by the US (ST/SG/SER.E/400); now Omnispace's OMNI-M1, operated under FCC experimental authority (47 CFR Part 5)

instruments.name: Registration by the United States, ST/SG/SER.E/400 (2001-026A)
instruments.note: US registered 2001-026A (launched 19 Jun 2001, MEO ~10,390 km).

instruments.name: Communications Act of 1934, as amended, 47 U.S.C. § 151 et seq. (esp. §§ 301, 303, 308-310)
instruments.note: Statutory basis for FCC licensing of US space stations (s.301 licence requirement; s.310(b) foreign-ownership limits). FCC authorises Omnispace LLC's use of the F2 satellite (experimental/STA grants,

instruments.name: 47 C.F.R. Part 5 – Experimental Radio Service
instruments.note: Basis of FCC experimental licences and STAs for Omnispace testing with the F2 satellite.

instruments.name: 47 C.F.R. Part 25 – Satellite Communications
instruments.note: FCC space-station licensing rules incl. orbital-debris showings (s.25.114(d)(14)) and disposal (s.25.283); to sunset when Part 100 takes effect.

instruments.name: FCC Report and Order and FNPRM, Space Modernization for the 21st Century, FCC 26-47 (SB Docket No. 25-306) – new 47 C.F.R. Part 100
instruments.note: Adopted 22 Jul 2026: replaces Part 25 with Part 100 (licensing 'assembly line', milestones, debris certifications). Effective date to be set by Space Bureau public notice.

instruments.name: Secure Space Act of 2026, S. 1962, 119th Congress (companion: Secure Space Act of 2025, H.R. 2458)
instruments.note: Would bar FCC satellite licences/market access for Covered-List entities. S.1962 passed Senate 23 Sep 2026 (engrossed); H.R.2458 passed House. Not enacted.

considered_not_relevant.name: Land Remote Sensing Policy Act (51 U.S.C. ch. 601) and 15 C.F.R. Part 960
considered_not_relevant.reason: NOAA private remote-sensing licensing; system is communications-only, no EO payload.

considered_not_relevant.name: Export control (ITAR, 22 C.F.R. Parts 120-130; EAR)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Controls technology transfer, not authorisation or supervision of the space objects.

USBZ.borderline: Commercial satellite built by US Loral for a Brazilian subsidiary; code reflects US/Brazil involvement. Brazil is State of registry; US role limited to launch licensing.
USBZ.instrument: Sole object Estrela do Sul 1 / Telstar 14 (2004-001A), owner Telesat Brasil, registered by Brazil (ST/SG/SER.E/678; reorbited to disposal 17 Nov 2011); launched by Sea Launch under FAA licence (51 U.S.C. ch. 509)

instruments.name: Registration by Brazil, ST/SG/SER.E/678 (Estrela do Sul 1)
instruments.note: Brazil registered EdS1 (owner Telesat Brasil Capacidade de Satélites Ltda); notes reorbit to disposal orbit 17 Nov 2011.

instruments.name: Resolução Anatel nº 748, de 22 de outubro de 2021 – Regulamento Geral de Exploração de Satélites (Brazil), as amended
instruments.note: Anatel right-to-exploit-satellite regime for Brazilian satellites (replacing earlier rules under Lei 9.472/1997); amended incl. by Res. 777/2025.

instruments.name: Lei nº 14.946, de 31 de julho de 2024 – atividades espaciais nacionais (Brazil)
instruments.note: Current Brazilian licensing law; post-dates EdS1's operations.

instruments.name: Portaria AEB nº 96, de 30 de novembro de 2011 – Registro de objetos espaciais (Brazil)
instruments.note: National registry of space objects kept by AEB.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Act, 51 U.S.C. ch. 509 (Commercial Space Launch Activities)
instruments.note: FAA-licensed Sea Launch mission (Zenit-3SL from Odyssey platform, 10/11 Jan 2004); US launch licensing and financial responsibility.

COL.instrument: No space licensing law; Colombian Space Commission (Decree 2442 of 2006, amended by Decree 184 of 2023); satellites under ICT Law 1341 of 2009; AESCOL agency bill (PL 179/2025 Senate) not enacted

instruments.name: Law 1341 of 2009 (ICT Law), as amended by Law 1978 of 2019
instruments.note: MinTIC/ANE spectrum permits, including for satellite services; the only route by which satellites are authorised.

instruments.name: Decree 2442 of 2006 (creates the Colombian Space Commission – CCE)
instruments.note: Inter-institutional coordination and advisory body for space policy; no licensing power.

instruments.name: Decree 184 of 10 February 2023 (amends Art. 3 of Decree 2442 of 2006)
instruments.note: Changes the CCE's composition, moving its presidency to the Presidency of the Republic.

instruments.name: Bill No. 179 of 2025 Senate (creates the Space Agency of the Republic of Colombia – AESCOL)
instruments.note: Filed by MinDefensa 19 Aug 2025; first debate postponed in Senate First Committee (May 2026); no approval found. May have lapsed at end of 2025-26 session. Agency only.

EST.instrument: No space act in force; draft Space Act (Kosmoseseadus, EIS 24-0963) consulted 2024-25 and submitted to the Government in Aug 2026; spectrum under the Electronic Communications Act

instruments.name: Elektroonilise side seadus (Electronic Communications Act)
instruments.note: Frequency authorisations and ITU satellite filings (TTJA). This is the only licensing that currently applies to Estonian satellites.

instruments.name: Kosmoseseaduse eelnõu (draft Space Act), EIS dossier 24-0963
instruments.note: MKM draft. Inter-ministerial rounds Sep 2024 and May 2025; submitted to the Government Aug 2026. Not yet in the Riigikogu.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

BOL.instrument: No space licensing law; Supreme Decree No. 0423 (2010) creates the Bolivian Space Agency (ABE, State satellite operator); satellite services under Law No. 164 of 2011

instruments.name: Supreme Decree No. 0423 of 10 February 2010 (creates the Agencia Boliviana Espacial – ABE)
instruments.note: Creates ABE as a State public enterprise to run the Túpac Katari satellite programme; State operation, no private authorisation regime.

instruments.name: Law No. 164 of 8 August 2011 (General Law on Telecommunications and ICT)
instruments.note: ATT licensing of spectrum and satellite services; telecom only.

URY.instrument: No space activities law; 2022 Uruguayan Space Agency bill (Carpeta 3275/2022) still in committee; 101-article space policy bill approved in Cabinet (Sept 2026), not yet sent to Parliament; satellites regulated by URSEC

instruments.name: Law No. 17,296 of 2001 (creates URSEC, arts. 70 ff.)
instruments.note: URSEC regulates and licenses spectrum use, including satellite services; telecom only.

instruments.name: Bill creating the Agencia Espacial Uruguaya (Carpeta No. 3275/2022, Repartido No. 70, Chamber of Representatives)
instruments.note: Executive bill of 20 Dec 2022 for an agency to authorise and supervise non-governmental space activities. Re-distributed in Defence Committee Mar 2025; not enacted.

instruments.name: Draft Space Policy Law (MIEM, 101 articles)
instruments.note: Presented to the Council of Ministers in Sept 2026; would create a licensing system for satellites, exploration and space tourism. Not yet sent to Parliament.

IRAQ.instrument: No national space law; satellite services licensed by the Communications and Media Commission under CPA Order No. 65 (2004), incl. Regulations for licensing terrestrial stations for space services (July 2024)

instruments.name: Coalition Provisional Authority Order No. 65 (2004) establishing the Communications and Media Commission
instruments.note: Legal basis (ss. 3 and 5) for CMC spectrum and telecom licensing, incl. satellite services.

instruments.name: CMC Regulations for licensing terrestrial stations for space services (First Issue, July 2024; Commissioners' Council Decision No. 78 of 23/7/2024)
instruments.note: Licensing of earth stations (FSS, MSS, ESIM, NGSO access) in Iraq; ground segment only, not space objects.

TMMC.borderline: Neither State was party to OST/LIAB/REG as at 1 Jan 2025 (Monaco: OST signature only); satellite not UN-registered. Turkmen law number (input: 307-V) not verified.
TMMC.instrument: Sole object TurkmenAlem52E/MonacoSAT (2015-023A): Turkmen State satellite using a Monaco ITU filing (Space Systems International–Monaco). Turkmenistan: Law 'On Space Activity' (2015); Monaco: draft space law

instruments.name: Law of Turkmenistan 'On Space Activity' (2015)
instruments.note: Framework law adopted by the Mejlis in 2015 (scope, principles, prohibitions, national space programme); licensing content not verified from official text.

instruments.name: Commercial Space Launch Act, 51 U.S.C. ch. 509 (Commercial Space Launch Activities)
instruments.note: Launched on Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral (27 Apr 2015) under FAA launch licence.

instruments.name: Monaco draft law on space activities (prepared with UNOOSA 'Space Law for New Space Actors' assistance, 2024)
instruments.note: Monaco's Office for Outer Space Affairs drafting a space-activities law and preparing treaty accession; not enacted as verified.

LAOS.borderline: Decree 471/GOL (2019) requires Lao legal entities that establish or buy satellites to register with the telecom ministry, which then files with the ITU (Art 21). This is a satellite-communications and spectrum registration, not an authorisation of space activities.
LAOS.instrument: No space act. Satellite communications, including satellite registration for ITU filing and operator permits, fall under Decree on Satellite Communications No. 471/GOL (2019), based on the Law on Radio Frequency (2017)

instruments.name: Decree on Satellite Communications, No. 471/GOL, dated 27 December 2019
instruments.note: Allocates satellite frequencies and orbits; entities establishing Lao satellites apply to register with the ministry for ITU filing (Arts 21-23); permits for satellite services and earth stations.

instruments.name: Law on Radio Frequency No. 17/NA, dated 5 May 2017
instruments.note: Parent law for spectrum and orbit management, cited in the Decree 471 preamble. Standalone official text not fetched.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law on Telecommunications (2011)
considered_not_relevant.reason: General telecom licensing. Satellite matters are governed specifically by Decree 471/GOL.

BGD.instrument: No space act. Satellite services are licensed by the BTRC under the Bangladesh Telecommunication Act 2001 (Act No. XVIII of 2001), amended by Act No. 51 of 2026. SPARRSO Act 1991 is institutional only

instruments.name: Bangladesh Telecommunication Act, 2001 (Act No. XVIII of 2001), formerly the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Act, 2001
instruments.note: BTRC licensing of telecom, radio and satellite-communication services and spectrum. Applies to artificial satellites. Not an Art VI authorisation regime.

instruments.name: Bangladesh Telecommunication (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 51 of 2026)
instruments.note: Dated 10 Apr 2026, deemed in force 5 Feb 2026; repeals Ordinance No. 25 of 2026. Drops 'Regulatory' from the Act's title; adds satellite equipment/services provisions and satellite-jamming offences.

instruments.name: Bangladesh Space Research and Remote Sensing Organization Act, 1991 (Act No. 29 of 1991)
instruments.note: Establishes SPARRSO for space research and remote sensing. It confers no power to license or register private space activities.

considered_not_relevant.name: Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 (Ordinance No. 25 of 2026)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Repealed and replaced by Act No. 51 of 2026.

considered_not_relevant.name: BTRC guidelines for NGSO satellite service operators (2025)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Service-licensing guidelines for satellite internet, not space-object authorisation. The official text could not be fetched because btrc.gov.bd was unreachable.

JOR.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellite and spectrum licensing by the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission under Telecommunications Law No. 13 of 1995 (as amended)

instruments.name: Telecommunications Law No. 13 of 1995 (as amended)
instruments.note: TRC spectrum management and licensing incl. satellite services and ITU filings; no space-object authorisation regime.

GRSA.borderline: Greece is licensing/registering State. Saudi Arabia (party to OST/LIAB/REG) co-owns via KACST; Saudi space instruments not verified. Law 4508 cited via lawspot (official FEK site unreachable).
GRSA.instrument: Sole object Hellas Sat 4/SGS-1 (2019-007A), shared by Hellas Sat (Arabsat group) and KACST; registered by Greece (ST/SG/SER.E/1044) under Law 4508/2017 on licensing of space activities and the national registry

instruments.name: Law 4508/2017 – Licensing of space activities; entry in the National Registry of Space Objects; establishment of the Hellenic Space Agency (Greece)
instruments.note: Published 21 Dec 2017: licensing, liability and supervision of space activities (Art. 1(1)(a)) and national registry (Art. 1(1)(b)); agency provisions later superseded.

instruments.name: Registration by Greece, ST/SG/SER.E/1044 (Hellas Sat-3 & Hellas Sat-4)
instruments.note: Greece registered Hellas Sat 4 (combined HS-4/SGS-1).

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final
instruments.note: Commission proposal (June 2025) for EU-wide authorisation, registration and safety/debris rules, incl. for third-country operators serving the EU; in legislative procedure.

ETH.instrument: No space-activities licensing law; SSGI established under Proclamation No. 1263/2021 with powers set by Council of Ministers Regulation No. 511/2022; spectrum under Proclamation No. 1148/2019

instruments.name: Communication Service Proclamation No. 1148/2019
instruments.note: Ethiopian Communications Authority licenses communication services and spectrum, incl. satellite.

instruments.name: Definition of Powers and Duties of the Executive Organs Proclamation No. 1263/2021
instruments.note: Places the Space Science and Geospatial Institute (SSGI) among executive organs.

instruments.name: Space Science and Geospatial Institute Establishment Council of Ministers Regulation No. 511/2022
instruments.note: Sets SSGI powers (space science, geospatial and satellite programmes); no private licensing regime identified.

considered_not_relevant.name: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024
considered_not_relevant.reason: Data protection; no space-object authorisation function.

NKOR.borderline: The Law on Space Development (2013, revised Aug 2022) regulates design, launch and operation of satellites through NADA. However, all space actors are State organs; there is no authorisation of non-governmental entities (State monopoly). No official full text is available online, only KCNA reporting. Hence 'no' under the strict rule.
NKOR.instrument: Law of the DPRK on Space Development (SPA, 1 April 2013; revised Aug 2022) establishing NADA; national registry notified to UN (ST/SG/SER.E/INF/31, 2015). State monopoly, no private authorisation

instruments.name: Law of the DPRK on Space Development
instruments.note: Adopted by SPA 1 Apr 2013. Revised by SPA Standing Committee Aug 2022 (adds defence purposes). Covers satellite design to operation under NADA. No official online text; cited via KCNA report.

instruments.name: Notification of establishment of a national registry (ST/SG/SER.E/INF/31, note verbale of 26 Feb 2015)
instruments.note: DPRK notified the UN of its national registry, with NADA as focal point. UN registrations: ST/SG/SER.E/662 (2013) and 768 (2016).

SVK.instrument: Act No. 378/2024 Coll. on the regulation of space activities (in force 1 February 2025): Ministry of Transport authorisation and supervision, national register of space objects

instruments.name: Zákon č. 378/2024 Z. z. o regulácii vesmírnych aktivít a o zmene a doplnení zákona NR SR č. 145/1995 Z. z. o správnych poplatkoch (Act No. 378/2024 Coll. on the regulation of space activities)
instruments.note: Adopted 28 Nov 2024; in force 1 Feb 2025. Permits for regulated space activities, State supervision and safety, and a national register of space objects at the Ministry of Transport.

instruments.name: Zákon č. 452/2021 Z. z. o elektronických komunikáciách (Electronic Communications Act)
instruments.note: Frequency authorisations and ITU satellite filings.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

HRV.instrument: No dedicated space activities law; satellite networks and spectrum regulated by HAKOM under the Electronic Communications Act (NN 76/2022, as amended)

instruments.name: Zakon o elektroničkim komunikacijama (Electronic Communications Act), Narodne novine 76/2022, as amended
instruments.note: Frequency licensing and ITU satellite filings by HAKOM. This is the only licensing that applies to Croatian satellites.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.

DJI.instrument: Law No. 167/AN/22/8ème L of 10 Nov 2022 on launch, flight operation and guidance of space objects, with Decree No. 2023-209/PR/MENSUR on the authorisation procedure and technical rules

instruments.name: Loi n° 167/AN/22/8ème L relative aux activités de lancement, d'opération de vol et de guidage d'objets spatiaux
instruments.note: JO No. 21, 15 Nov 2022. Prior ministerial authorisation (Art. 3), conditions incl. insurance (Art. 4), transfer control, national register (Arts 10-12), State recourse (Art. 13).

instruments.name: Décret n° 2023-209/PR/MENSUR fixant la procédure d'autorisation d'opérations de lancement ou de guidage d'objets spatiaux
instruments.note: JO No. 14, 31 Jul 2023. Application dossier and technical rules: debris limits, collision avoidance, disposal, re-entry safety, constellations, in-orbit servicing.

BWA.instrument: No space law, space agency or space policy in force; spectrum and satellite communications regulated by BOCRA under the Communications Regulatory Authority Act, 2012

instruments.name: Communications Regulatory Authority Act, 2012
instruments.note: BOCRA licenses spectrum and communications services incl. satellite; no authorisation regime for space objects (BOTSAT-1 launched 2025 without a space law).

BHR.instrument: No enacted space law; National Space Law (licensing, liability, spectrum, debris) under development by the Bahrain Space Agency (est. by Decree No. 11 of 2014, reorganised 2025); spectrum via TRA

instruments.name: Telecommunications Law promulgated by Legislative Decree No. (48) of 2002
instruments.note: TRA spectrum and telecom licensing; BSA coordinates ITU frequency/orbit filings with TRA.

instruments.name: Decree No. (11) of 2014 establishing the National Space Science Agency, as amended (incl. Decree No. (14) of 2025)
instruments.note: Establishes NSSA, renamed Bahrain Space Agency; amended 2019, 2024, 2025. Agency law only.

instruments.name: Royal Order No. (18) of 2025 reorganizing the Bahrain Space Agency
instruments.note: Reorganises BSA governance; no licensing regime.

instruments.name: Draft National Space Law of the Kingdom of Bahrain
instruments.note: BSA states it is developing a National Space Law covering licensing, liability, spectrum and debris; no bill text published.

considered_not_relevant.name: Law No. (13) of 2019 approving accession to the Outer Space Treaty
considered_not_relevant.reason: Treaty accession act; no domestic authorisation or registry mechanism.

SLB.instrument: No space act. The Telecommunications Commission (TCSI) handles satellite filings and spectrum under the Telecommunications Act 2009 (No. 20 of 2009), e.g. the SI-SAT networks

instruments.name: Telecommunications Act 2009 (No. 20 of 2009)
instruments.note: Passed 27 Aug 2009. TCSI allocates and assigns spectrum, including satellite, and administers ITU satellite filings (SI-SAT-Kurukuru, SI-SAT-Bilikiki). Spectrum only.

NZ.instrument: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities Act 2017 (launch, payload, facility and high-altitude licences/permits; liability) as amended by the Amendment Act 2025; Licences and Permits Regulations 2017

instruments.name: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities Act 2017 (2017 No 29)
instruments.note: Launch licences, payload permits, facility licences, overseas launch licences, high-altitude licences (MBIE/NZ Space Agency); orbital debris conditions; Crown indemnity/liability recovery.

instruments.name: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities Amendment Act 2025 (2025 No 38)
instruments.note: Amends the 2017 Act, incl. regulation of ground-based space infrastructure per the prior dataset. Text and commencement could not be fetched (site bot-blocked); unverified.

instruments.name: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities (Licences and Permits) Regulations 2017 (LI 2017/250)
instruments.note: Application information, fees and criteria for licences and payload permits (e.g. orbital debris mitigation plans).

instruments.name: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities (Definition of High-altitude Vehicle) Regulations 2017 (LI 2017/251)
instruments.note: Defines high-altitude vehicles subject to licensing under the Act.

considered_not_relevant.name: Radiocommunications Act 1989 (RSM spectrum licensing)
considered_not_relevant.reason: Spectrum/ITU filings only; space authorisation is under the 2017 Act. Relevant only as a background frequency-coordination regime.

MNE.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellite spectrum and communications regulated by EKIP under the Law on Electronic Communications

instruments.name: Zakon o elektronskim komunikacijama (Law on Electronic Communications), Službeni list CG 100/24, as amended
instruments.note: Frequency licensing and ITU coordination by EKIP. This is the only licensing that applies to satellites under Montenegrin jurisdiction.

ROM.instrument: No space activities authorisation law; Law No. 380/2022 (accession to the Registration Convention) tasks ROSA with setting up and keeping the national registry of space objects

instruments.name: Legea nr. 380/2022 pentru aderarea României la Convenția privind înmatricularea obiectelor lansate în spațiul extra-atmosferic (Law No. 380 of 28 December 2022)
instruments.note: Accession to the Registration Convention. ROSA is designated to set up and keep the national registry. No licensing of private operators.

instruments.name: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the safety, resilience and sustainability of space activities in the Union (EU Space Act), COM(2025) 335 final, 2025/0335(COD)
instruments.note: Commission proposal 25 Jun 2025. Still pending: EP ITRE at committee stage (draft report Mar 2026); Council only a progress report (May 2026), no general approach. Would add an EU authorisation layer.
